articles.body: LeBron James, the former Los Angeles Lakers’ star player, has kept his focus on the last season in court as he is all set to retire after the upcoming season. While LeBron James gears up to play for the Philadelphia 76ers, he has remained passionate about Akron. Amid this, LeBron James’ comments on his roots in Akron have moved many.LeBron James reflects on his love and dedication for Akron and growing up there in a middle class homeIn an interview with the Los Angeles Times’ Dan Woike, the four time NBA champion, LeBron James opened up about his love for Akron as he said, “People always say, ‘You’re going back home.’ But I tell people all the time, ‘I’m not from Cleveland.’”The star player added, “There’s no disrespect to Cleveland. But, when you’re from Akron, you’re not from Cleveland,” James told Woike. “This is where I’m from.”LeBron James also reflected on the childhood he has had in Akron as he said, “When you grow up in Akron, Ohio, you already feel like no one cares about you too much,” he said. “And the only people that really care about you are the ones from that town.”He added, “When you are in certain community centers, in certain gyms, you look for inspiration—people who came before you, people who were already there.”LeBron James has continuously worked towards Akron’s developments and changed thousands of lives thereIn the last two decades, as and when LeBron James’ wealth grew after being drafted in the league, he remained loyal to his hometown and has continued to donate.Apart from his foundations, LeBron James has also been there for his alma mater, St. Vincent–St. Mary High School, as he funded a $1 million renovation for the school’s gym.While St. Vincent–St. Mary basketball has continued to add new talents, LeBron James reflected on it as he said, “It means you set the path along the way while you’re doing it for the next generation. It was our whole thing while we were there…”The four time NBA champion added, “It started with Maverick [Carter] and Derrick and Darren Tarver, guys who were there already. articles.title: Why Kawhi Leonard sat out Raptors’ preseason game as Heat dominated in Quebec City
articles.summary: Miami Heat secured a stunning and dominating win in Quebec City on Saturday, and Kawhi Leonard never made it onto the floor in the Raptors' preseason
articles.body: Miami Heat secured a stunning and dominating win in Quebec City on Saturday, and Kawhi Leonard never made it onto the floor in the Raptors' preseason opener. Raptors coach Darko Rajakovic had hinted at the outcome a day earlier, then confirmed it before tipoff at Videotron Centre. Miami led 120-101 with about two minutes left.Toronto describes the absence as a planned ramp-up after a long summer on hold, and the schedule stretches well past one night. Even the Oct. 10 game against the Clippers in Vancouver looks like a long shot.Why Kawhi Leonard did not play for the Raptors against the Heat in Quebec CityKawhi Leonard sat out because the Raptors are rebuilding his conditioning after a long summer on hold, and the team says no new injury is involved. Rajakovic told reporters before tipoff that Leonard would not face the Heat at Videotron Centre. He also said Leonard likely misses the Oct. 10 game in Vancouver. “The Raptors have been taking it slow with the oft-injured Leonard in camp, a very light head-to-head drill between the coach and the superstar after Friday's practice notwithstanding. He has yet to participate in full-contact drills," according to The Canadian Press.Leonard moved from the Clippers to Toronto in June, but the deal stalled for most of the summer while the NBA examined salary-cap circumvention involving the player and the Clippers. Rajakovic ties the long layoff directly to that pause.Leonard helped Toronto win its first NBA championship in 2019. Last season with the Clippers produced 27.9 points and 3.6 assists per game over 65 appearances, plus a spot on the All-NBA second team.The 35-year-old forward has worked through drills at practice but has not joined full-contact sessions. Leonard also skipped the intrasquad scrimmage, and the Raptors keep calling the whole process reconditioning.Rajakovic offered a lighter moment after Friday's practice, joking that Leonard had earned a game against the Heat by winning a light one-on-one. The drill was light, and the plan stayed as it was. The coach was more serious about the bigger picture, calling the situation "a day-to-day thing with Kawhi."How the Heat pulled away and what comes next for Kawhi LeonardWithout Leonard, Toronto spent most of the night chasing. Miami dropped 41 points on the Raptors in the opening quarter and carried an 18-point lead into the second. The second quarter was closer, 35-32 in Miami's favor, though the damage was done by then. By halftime, the Heat were up 76-55.The Raptors won the third quarter 25-19, trimming the gap to 15 heading into the fourth. Miami had added 25 more by the time the clock showed 2:11, with the score at 120-101. Both teams are 0-0, so the score only reflects the preseason. Finally, the Heat secured 129-105 win.TSN's Josh Lewenberg reported that Leonard is expected to miss the first two preseason games, a stretch that covers the Oct. 10 meeting with the Clippers in Vancouver.Toronto enters the 2026-27 season with real expectations and has been open about prioritizing a gradual buildup for Leonard. If the plan holds, Leonard still has three preseason chances to play before the regular season starts.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 6-foot-9 Luka Doncic’s Lakers teammate makes romantic move with longtime girlfriend at Bruno Mars Concert
articles.summary: Ziaire Williams went to SoFi Stadium on Friday night for a Bruno Mars show, but the Lakers wing had a bigger plan than singing along.
articles.body: Ziaire Williams went to SoFi Stadium on Friday night for a Bruno Mars show, but the Lakers wing had a bigger plan than singing along. Mars and the stadium crew both appeared to be in on it.The song was "Marry You," and Williams used it to propose to his girlfriend while cameras rolled. The video board carried the moment to the stadium, and fans soon passed the clip around online. The Lakers have not even opened the preseason yet, which makes it the first big headline of their new season.Ziaire Williams proposes to girlfriend at Bruno Mars concertZiaire Williams picked a stadium concert for a question that usually gets asked in private. The proposal came on Friday night at SoFi Stadium, right as Bruno Mars performed "Marry You." Mars and the stadium staff appeared to know the surprise was coming. Cameras caught the moment, and the video board put it in front of the crowd so everyone could celebrate with the couple.The song choice did half the work. Few tracks announce the question as clearly as "Marry You," and the crowd had an easy cue to cheer.SoFi Stadium posted its own reaction on X. "It really was a beautiful night 🥹💍," the venue wrote, tagging Mars. Fan video spread as well. A post from @MrBuckBuckNBA, sharing a clip from @Kjblazin, read:“Ziaire Williams just proposed to his girlfriend at the Bruno mars concert. Way to start your journey with the Lakers.”The night also fits a busy summer for Williams. He joined the Lakers a few months ago, a move that brought the 25-year-old home and set up a reunion with high school teammate Bronny James.Williams turns attention to Lakers camp and a starting roleThe calendar did not leave much room for a victory lap. The Lakers went back to the practice court on Saturday and open a five-game preseason slate on Monday, on the road against the Sacramento Kings. Williams is one of the players competing for a starting spot, so this camp carries real weight for the wing.Memphis drafted Williams, and Brooklyn gave the wing the last two seasons. At Lakers media day, Williams talked about wanting to be in a winning environment. "I play to win, right?" Williams said. The mindset came from Williams' father, who taught the value of competing whatever the stat sheet says.The standard in Los Angeles is a championship, Williams said of Luka Doncic's team, and the wing is fully on board with that goal. Winning at home, with family and friends in the building, carries extra meaning.A bigger role could follow. articles.title: Dream's defensive showcase, led by Angel Reese, stymies Liberty in Game 1 of WNBA semifinals: '[DPOY] is in Atlanta for a reason'
articles.summary: Angel Reese was named Defensive Player of the Year this week, and Sunday's performance in Game 1 showed exactly why.
articles.body:
ATLANTA — Angel Reese keeps her vision board to herself and checks off items as the season progresses. She knocked off Defensive Player of the Year this month , one of the items listed at the bottom as one of her individual aspirations, and accepted the trophy in front of the home fans on Sunday.

When she did, she added a task to a to-do list: she intends to engrave it with the names of Atlanta Dream teammates Jordin Canada and Rhyne Howard. She's been saying for weeks now that any of the three league leaders in steals were worthy of the award.

Few would argue with that in the aftermath of a 92-82 win over the No. 8 New York Liberty in Game 1 of the WNBA semifinals on Sunday. No one who watched the third-quarter suffocation of two former MVPs and an all-WNBA guard, specifically, would dissent.

"It goes to show," Angel Reese told a group of reporters post-game. "Defensive Player of the Year is in Atlanta for a reason."

The Dream snatched balls out of bellies and smacked them out of the air. In the second quarter, Reese denied Sabrina Ionescu at the rim and delivered a staredown to an amped courtside crowd. In one third-quarter sequence, Canada played swiper three times in a row. Collectively, they smothered a team that still starts four players from their 2024 championship team.

The Liberty couldn't sniff a whiff of the paint if it were a perfume store. Atlanta locked them out, forcing drivers wide and shots off target. The Dream fully shut the door in a deafening third quarter that should rattle the thought of a Liberty Finals.

New York led 40-37 at the half. It was a grind of a game, but one they could break through. They were shooting better (43.8%) than the Dream (34.3%) and began to find their groove offensively, allowing Breanna Stewart to pull up in the mid-range and Pauline Astier to drive.

DeWanna Bonner, a rare late-season acquisition who's already one of the best midseason signings of the decade, lit into her young, inexperienced roster. Reese, Howard and Allisha Gray, who sustained a hand injury and only played 10:47, are playing in their first semifinals. Bonner notched postseason game No. 101 on Sunday. She declined to divulge exactly what she said.

Canada, who won two titles with Stewart and Sue Bird in Seattle in her first and third seasons, shared the basics. They needed a second-half surge that started in the first three minutes of the quarter.

"It started defensively with our energy," Canada said. "We were able to get stops and get out in transition, which is what we do best, and from there we were able to separate a little bit and finish off."

It was a return to the unfancy, yet no less skilled, bread and butter that carried them here. They turned the Liberty over nine times in the frame for 16 points, more than the Liberty's 15 points as a team. New York shot 42.9% from the perimeter with three 3s, but 1 of 7 from inside the arc (14%). Jones and Stewart, with their inside presence, combined to shoot 1 of 4. The Dream pounded the paint (18-2), won in transition (11-0) and off second chances (5-0).

Canada, the veteran point guard, came back from early foul trouble — "I might have been a little bit too handsy," she admitted — finished the game with a team-high five steals, 25 points and even a block. Reese had four steals and three blocks, along with 17 points, 7 rebounds, 2 assists and 4 turnovers. Howard scored 16 with a team-high eight assists. Bonner had 23 points, going 10 of 18 and 3 of 6 from 3. Each had one steal, as six of nine players who saw the court stole it at least once.

One-third of Atlanta's total offense came from points off turnovers. They turned the Liberty over 21 times — nearly identical to the 20 they had in two of their three regular-season games against Atlanta — for 32 points. It tied the WNBA postseason record for points off turnovers.

"We'll go back and watch the film and just understand those points off turnovers really mattered, especially on a team that feeds off of it," Ionescu said.

An understatement of the century. Ionescu, Stewart and first-year head coach Chris DeMarco all said afterward they knew Atlanta's favorite meal. They were aware that live-ball turnovers would be key. It was the question posed to them all week leading into their semifinal appearance as a No. 8 seed, the first to do so in league history. Stewart noted the Dream did this exact same thing two weeks ago in the regular season.

Left unsaid: They couldn't do anything about it.

"We need to be better," Stewart said. "We need to be more prepared and expect that."

Atlanta successfully set the semifinals' tone in the franchise's first appearance since 2018. The Dream, which came into the league as a 2008 expansion team, has never won a championship despite reaching the Finals three times in four years between 2010 and 2013. They finished the regular season as one of the league's best defensive units, limiting the fastbreak and second-chance points. They averaged a league-high 9.1 steals per game.

They've upped it in the playoffs. Rarely could New York beat them back on offense, forcing the Liberty to fight for every inch. Not even Stewart, the three-time WNBA champion too often dragging this Liberty team to success, could save them with a late flurry. A steal-and-score pulled the Liberty to within five with 2:50 to play. It was the third time in 2:30 of game time they pulled as close. Atlanta led by as many as 16.

On her way back down the court's sideline, Reese yelled and motioned "settle down" with a purpose. She told head coach Karl Smesko to call a timeout. He obliged.

In red carpet-worthy street clothes, her Defensive Player of the Year trophy safe in the bowels of State Farm Arena, Reese said she felt the team was getting too high and needed to regroup.

"We wanted to make sure we were better than that, because this is the playoffs," Reese said. "Anybody can come back, and especially in this environment. If this was in New York, I mean, it could have went another way, especially with their crowd into it."

The three-game series made Reese nervous. Anything can happen in those, she said. A five-game series gives more of a runway, which DeMarco said he will take as the Liberty make those adjustments for Game 2 on Wednesday.

"I don't want to dictate and rely on five games," Reese said. "I want to be able to win, win, win, win, win and move onto the next round. That's kind of how the mindset has been."

To reach the playoffs for the first time in her three-year career was technically on her goal sheet. But she said she knew she would reach it playing for the Dream, the team that traded for her on the dawn of an abbreviated offseason window. Clinching the semifinals proved the franchise could get over the hump after Howard, Gray and Canada lost in the first round a year ago.

At the top of the vision board are team goals, led by the one she said earlier on Sunday would mean more than DPOY: a WNBA championship. They're one defensive showcase closer to it.

articles.title: LA Clippers injury update: 6-foot-5 star hit with concerning news in preseason opener vs Golden State Warriors
articles.summary: Max Strus was five minutes into his Clippers debut when a routine cut turned ugly.
articles.body: Max Strus was five minutes into his Clippers debut when a routine cut turned ugly. The 6-foot-5 forward came off a screen, caught a pass from Darius Garland, and hopped away from the play on one leg. Coach Ty Lue called a timeout. Strus walked to the locker room and never came back to the preseason opener against the Golden State Warriors.Reports point to a right foot problem, and the Clippers have not offered a diagnosis. Brandon Ingram is already sidelined for the start of the season, and opening night is about three weeks away.Max Strus injury update: What happened in the Clippers' preseason openerMax Strus went down on Sunday night with a little over seven minutes left in the first quarter. The play itself looked ordinary. Strus ran off a screen with Stephen Curry chasing him, took the pass from Garland on the wing, and seemed to tweak something right after the catch. He hopped on the left foot to get away from the action. No other player was close enough to blame, so this looks like a non-contact injury.Lue stopped the game, and Strus went to see the team doctors. Clippers reporter Joey Linn relayed that the forward would not return with a right foot injury. Other accounts of the play call it a right ankle issue, which means the exact problem is still unclear.Strus played five minutes, grabbed one rebound, and missed the lone shot he took. Rookie Keaton Wagler picked up most of the minutes left behind, while Rui Hachimura, Derrick Jones Jr. and Cam Christie also saw larger roles.Why the Strus injury could hurt the Clippers' seasonStrus was likely headed for a first-half cap anyway, since teams usually go easy in preseason. That does not explain the limp. Foot trouble has followed him before. Last season with the Cleveland Cavaliers, Strus missed the first 67 games while recovering from a fractured left foot and finished with only 12 appearances. In those games, he averaged 11.2 points, 5.4 rebounds and 2.0 assists, shooting 44.3 percent from the field and 40.2 percent from three.There is one encouraging detail. This time the right foot is involved, so it does not appear to be a flare-up of the old break. Strus arrived in August through a five-team trade centered on Peyton Watson, which makes this a first look at the fit that got cut short.The roster has little cushion. Ingram came over from the Toronto Raptors in the Kawhi Leonard trade, and nobody has a return date for him. The Leonard penalty also cost the Clippers their first-round picks, so a losing year would sting twice. articles.title: Nikola Jokić dazzles with behind-the-back pass down the baseline that you have to see to believe
articles.summary: Nikola Jokić is already doing Nikola Jokić things.
articles.body:
Nikola Jokić is already doing Nikola Jokić things.

The do-everything three-time MVP center was in action for the Denver Nuggets for a preseason game against the Utah Jazz Sunday night. Playing up the road from Denver on the University of Colorado's campus, Jokić uncorked this beauty for the Boulder home crowd.

Being able to imagine that pass to begin with is remarkable. There's probably nobody else in the NBA who would even think about it, much less consider executing it. And then Jokić did exactly just that.

He threw a no-look, behind the-back pass from one 3-point corner to the other directly down the baseline, bypassing three Jazz defenders in the process. Cam Johnson then made good on the sorcery, hoisting a catch-and-shoot 3-pointer that sank through the net.

Jokić, meanwhile, was already headed back on defense while Johnson's shot was in the air, correctly confident in the play's success.

It was a thing of basketball beauty from a meaningless basketball game that counts for nothing. But thankfully, it was caught on camera to inspire awe among the lovers of the game.

And soon enough, those passes will count. The Nuggets open their season in an Oct. 22 matchup against the Oklahoma City Thunder that will certainly matter.

LSU brought Wade back this spring and is hoping his second stint with the team will lead to the success the school has been after for years. After landing a top recruit on Sunday, it's safe to say Wade is building a competitive program.

articles.title: “I think we need another big”: Anthony Davis reveals how his genuine ask for roster change led to NBA shocker trade involving Luka Doncic in 2025
articles.summary: Anthony Davis got up to roughly 268 pounds in his last year with the Lakers, and the extra weight explains the request Davis made for another big man.
articles.body: Anthony Davis got up to roughly 268 pounds in his last year with the Lakers, and the extra weight explains the request Davis made for another big man. The NBA champion told the Wizards' Numbers on the Board podcast that the added pounds left him feeling "heavy."Playing center against Joel Embiid and Nikola Jokic at that size wore Davis down, and cutting weight midseason did not fix it. The Lakers never added a second big. Instead, they traded Davis to Dallas for Luka Doncic.Why Anthony Davis asked the Lakers for another big manThe ask came two weeks before the 2025 trade deadline. Anthony Davis told ESPN's Shams Charania that the Lakers needed a center to become real title contenders. The big man also wanted to go back to playing the four, the spot where the game fits best. "I think we need another big," Davis said.On the Wizards' Numbers on the Board podcast, Davis explained that usually played at 250 or 255 pounds. In his last year in Los Angeles, the scale climbed to 265 and maybe 268.The strength work was meant to prepare Davis for life at center, where natural centers like Joel Embiid and Nikola Jokic were beating Davis up night after night. Davis did not feel right in that body. "Bro, I can't play like this. I feel heavy," Davis said.Davis tried to cut weight during the season, but dropping pounds while still guarding centers every night was tough. He later sent a request to the front office. Nothing came of it. The Lakers did chase center Mark Williams from the Charlotte Hornets, but the trade was rescinded.The big request turned to a NBA shocker tradeThe Lakers answered with a trade nobody saw coming. Davis, Max Christie and a 2029 first-round pick went to the Mavericks for Doncic, Maxi Kleber and Markieff Morris. ESPN's Charania posted the deal, which also pulled in Utah. Jalen Hood-Schifino went to the Jazz to balance the money. Plenty of fans still call it the most shocking trade in NBA history.The weight problem traveled to Dallas. In the fall of 2025, Davis reported to Mavericks camp at 268 pounds, and fans got nervous. Further, an early calf strain limited him. Once the weight came off, the usual two-way game returned. In December, Davis put up 32 points and 13 rebounds against Jokic and the Nuggets.Davis has since been traded again, this time to Washington. The Wizards have Alex Sarr, Deandre Ayton, and Tristan Vukcevic, all able to play center, so the Wizards forward gets the starting power forward job he asked for in 2025. articles.body: Tobias Harris' injury update from San Antonio came with no timetable attached. Coach Mitch Johnson told reporters Sunday that the Spurs will let a left calf strain heal at its own pace, even with the season opener against the Oklahoma City Thunder on Oct. 20 getting close.San Antonio signed Harris this offseason to share the frontcourt with Victor Wembanyama, and his first camp has been interrupted by a strain with no firm return date. The $31 million forward sat out the weekend scrimmage and will be checked again once the preseason wraps up.Tobias Harris injury update: Spurs coach says there is no rush on the calf strainTobias Harris, 34, strained a left calf muscle in training camp, and the Spurs made the news public Sunday. The team lists Harris as questionable for the Oct. 20 opener and says a fresh evaluation will come after the preseason. Roughly two weeks separate the announcement from opening night.The Spurs announced the strain, Tom Orsborn of the San Antonio Express-News reported that Harris would not suit up for the scrimmage, and Johnson addressed it afterward at Frost Bank Center, "We won't rush him at all."The coach added that the staff sees no cause for alarm at this level of seriousness, though he stopped short of rating the strain. Asked about the opener, Johnson said Harris' availability is very much in doubt and the team will not push him toward that game. San Antonio has not given a return date or a number of weeks, so the next real update comes when Harris is reevaluated after the preseason, which opens Oct. 8 at home against the Atlanta Hawks and runs five games.How the Spurs lineup could look without himThe 6-foot-8 forward is not an easy piece to replace. Harris spent the past two seasons in Detroit, and last year the Pistons won 60 games and finished first in the East while Harris averaged 13.3 points, 5.1 rebounds and 2.5 assists over 63 appearances. Harris also shot 46.9% from the field and 36.8% from three in 27.7 minutes a night.San Antonio saw a big offseason pickup in those numbers. The idea was to add veteran presence and versatility to a team coming off a historic run to the 2026 NBA Finals. Harris was projected as the main frontcourt partner for Wembanyama, and the two-year, $31 million contract makes this more than a depth issue. Harris lists at small forward and power forward, so the injury touches more than one spot in the rotation.Without Harris, the Spurs will likely turn to the group that carried them last year, including Wembanyama, De'Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle, Devin Vassell and Julian Champagnie, with Dylan Harper coming off the bench. articles.summary: as Valkyries doblegan a las Aces y se adelantan 1-0 en las semifinales de la WNBA
articles.body: Las Golden State Valkyries doblegaron a Las Vegas Aces en el primer partido de las semifinales de la WNBA, jugadas al mejor de siete encuentros, al imponerse en casa por 71-60. Gabby Williams lideró la victoria con un gran doble doble de 25 puntos y 11 rebotes, con cinco de once desde el arco, apoyada por los once puntos de Kaitlyn Chen. Las Aces, que nunca había metido menos de 89 puntos en esta postemporada, tuvieron una noche complicada con el tiro. A'ja Wilson fue su líder anotadora con 24 puntos, Chelsea Gray metió 16 y Jackie Young no pasó de los once. El segundo partido de la serie se jugará el miércoles en San Francisco. En la otra semifinal, las Atlanta Dream tomaron ventaja gracias a un 92-82 en casa contra las New York Liberty. Las Dream fueron lideradas por 25 puntos de Jordin Canada y por 23 de DeWanna Bonner, mientras que Angel Reese contribuyó con 17 puntos y 7 rebotes. Las Liberty, que dieron la sorpresa en la primera ronda al eliminar a las Minnesota Lynx, pagaron un tercer cuarto perdido 32-15. Su máxima anotadora fue Sabrina Ionescu, con 27 puntos, y Breanna Stewart aportó 19 puntos. La española Raquel Carrera no jugó con las Liberty. Las Finales de la WNBA se disputarán a partir del 17 de octubre al mejor de 7 partidos.

articles.title: Payton Pritchard Could be Main Factor in Boston Celtics Success This Season
articles.summary: The sixth-year point guard will be tasked with navigating the team's re-tooled roster on the court.
articles.body:
The Boston Celtics will have a re-tooled roster this upcoming season, and question marks surrounding it.

The Celtics added multi-time All-Star wing Paul George, defending NBA champion and center Mitchell Robinson and veteran point guard Mike Conley this offseason, which a clear emphasis on improving the defensive capabilities of the team.

However, there's still a question over how the team will fit on offense.

Former NBA Finals MVP Jaylen Brown was traded to the Philadelphia 76ers this past offseason in return for George (and draft picks). Robinson will likely split time in the front court with Neemias Queta, who's coming off a career-best season and a contract extension.

And point guard Payton Pritchard will likely play a focal role in getting all the new pieces to fit together on offense.

Pritchard is coming off his sixth season in the NBA and the first as Boston's primary point guard after spending years as the team's sixth man, including winning the Sixth Man of the Year in 2025.

The former Oregon Duck posted his best season as a professional in the 2025-26 season. He averaged 17 points per game on 46.4% shooting from the floor (37.7% from 3-point range) across 79 games (50 starts). He also averaged 5.2 assists and 3.9 rebounds, both of which were career-highs.

Pritchard's growth as a scorer was important for the team, which was without superstar Jayson Tatum for the majority of the team. But his facilitating took a big jump even without Tatum in the fold.

Pritchard will enter this season as the team's starting point guard and will be backed up by one of the most respected veterans in the Association in Conley. This will allow Pritchard to manage the offense when Tatum doesn't have the ball in his hands. Conley coming off the bench will also allow the Celtics to maintain their defensive pressure when Pritchard isn't on the court.

Being able to make sure Queta continues his impact from his career-best season as the team's starting center while maximizing George and Robinson's impact on the offensive end of the court will be key for Boston to having the best results possible this upcoming season.

Pritchard, as the point guard of the offense, will be tasked as the floor general to make sure that happens.

The Celtics and Pritchard will play their first preseason game against the Cleveland Cavaliers at 7 p.m. ET on Oct. 8 at Rocket Arena in Cleveland.

articles.title: Angel Reese takes a shot at the Chicago Sky after winning WNBA DPOY award
articles.summary: Angel Reese took a dig at her former team, the Chicago Sky, after being named the 2026 WNBA Defensive Player of the Year. Angel Reese was named the Defensive...
articles.body:
Angel Reese took a dig at her former team, the Chicago Sky, after being named the 2026 WNBA Defensive Player of the Year.

Angel Reese was named the Defensive Player of the Year right before the Atlanta Dream's Game 1 clash in the Semifinals of the WNBA Playoffs. The 24-year-old was handed her trophy and she immediately showed why she deserves it with a dominant display in their 92-82 win.

Reese may be flying with the Dream, but they are not the team which drafted her. Coming in as one of women's basketball's biggest prospects, Reese was drafted by the Chicago Sky with the seventh overall pick in 2024. As she won her first major individual award, she had some words for her former team.

Angel Reese says 'she didn't have the opportunity' to show who she was in the WNBA for the past two years

Despite being named an All-Star in her first two seasons, Reese's time with the Sky was marked with failure. She never made the playoffs with them, and her offensive game was a big target for ridicule within the WNBA world. There were also reports of problems behind the scenes.

For any who may still have been in doubt about how Reese feels regarding her former employers, her words after winning the DPOY are an excellent look into how she feels about them.

"I knew who I was going to be coming into the league. Obviously, I didn't have the opportunity to do that in the past two years," Reese said. "Being able to come here to Atlanta, I knew what I was expected (to do); I knew that I was gonna be put on a pedestal of being able to play with great players… Being able to be here in Atlanta, just really grateful to have sisters in the locker room that genuinely care about me."

The Sky finished this season with a poor 16-28 record once again, missing out on the postseason by a wide margin. Now, their former star is taking shots at them as she succeeds in her very first season with another team. It is a tough time to be a Chicago fan.

articles.title: Atlanta's Ray Kerr got NLDS Game 2 start in the morning. At night, he struck out Shohei Ohtani
articles.summary: LOS ANGELES (AP) — Ray Kerr is becoming an unlikely postseason hero for the Atlanta Braves.The former convenience store and movie theater worker struck out f...
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — Ray Kerr is becoming an unlikely postseason hero for the Atlanta Braves .

The former convenience store and movie theater worker struck out four-time MVP Shohei Ohtani on a 95-mph four-seam fastball in the Braves' 3-2 victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers on Sunday night that evened their National League Division Series at a game apiece.

"He did it again for us, just amazing," Braves manager Walt Weiss said. "He's throwing the ball so well."

Ohtani was one of a season-high-tying four strikeouts for Kerr, a 32-year-old lefty reliever who found out in the morning that he'd be starting Game 2 that night. He allowed two hits and walked one in 2 2/3 innings.

"I didn't really have much pressure on me," Kerr said, explaining that he had breakfast with his wife and baby who are on the trip and went swimming. "And then when I got to the field, I developed my process in my head. Just an hour before the game, stretch, and get out there and only throw for like five, six minutes."

Kerr was the opener in the Braves' NL Wild Card Series Game 3 clincher over the Philadelphia Phillies, tossing 3 1/3 scoreless innings, with one hit, one walk and two strikeouts.

"It's been fun. It's very surprising," he said. "It's like one night, all of a sudden, I got a thousand followers on Instagram. I'm getting used to it. I'm just going to be myself throughout it."

At 13, Kerr landed in the foster care system in Reno, Nevada, because his father was in prison and his mother was absent. He and his brother were eventually taken in by a woman who provided the stability that had been lacking in their lives.

Kerr graduated from high school in Reno and played baseball at Mendocino College in Northern California for two years before quitting the sport. He returned home and took jobs at a 7-Eleven and a theater.

A coach at Lassen College in the Sierra Nevada foothills convinced Kerr to join the team. He went on to play in the Alaska Baseball League in 2017, where his fastball touched 93 mph. That August, he signed with the Seattle Mariners as an undrafted free agent.

In 2021, he was traded to the San Diego Padres. The following season he reached the majors for the first time, appearing in seven games before being sent down to Triple-A in 2023. Late that year, he was traded to the Braves and started the 2024 season at Triple-A.

He had Tommy John surgery, ending his season in June and keeping him out all of 2025. He returned this year and got selected to Atlanta's active roster in August.

Kerr made his season debut on Aug. 17, and posted a 1.47 ERA over 18 1/3 innings in nine appearances. Left-handed hitters — like Ohtani — hit .174 against him with a double being the only extra-base hit he allowed.

The Braves are headed back to Atlanta for Game 3 on Tuesday, when ace Chris Sale is expected to start.

"It's going to be crazy there," Kerr said. "The crowd's going to be beautiful to watch. I already know it. Especially against the Dodgers."

And if Kerr gets the nod to take down more innings again, he'll tell himself "All right, let's get it."

"That's what I say every time," he said, "and then I stick to it."

articles.title: Penguins Linked To $92.8 Million Star Forward
articles.summary: The discussion that fans of the Pittsburgh Penguins know is coming at some point is at least a full season away, but they won’t be able to ignore it much lon...
articles.body:
The discussion that fans of the Pittsburgh Penguins know is coming at some point is at least a full season away, but they won't be able to ignore it much longer.

The iconic duo of Sidney Crosby and Evgeni Malkin aren't getting any younger, and both players are going to call it a career sooner rather than later; right now, the prevailing thought is that 2026-27 could be the last year of Malkin's career, while Crosby is also entering the last year of his current contract.

The Penguins are going to need a reliable source of offense from a notable name to help carry the load when both players decide to hang up the skates, and right now, they're being named as having an outside shot to land an intriguing forward.

NHL Insider Links Pittsburgh Penguins To Canucks Forward Elias Pettersson

According to noted Vancouver Canucks insider Rick Dhaliwal, the Penguins have "some degree" of interest in Pettersson, though there's no current traction on any kind of deal.

"I do believe Pittsburgh has some degree of interest in Elias Pettersson. I am not hearing the rumour that the Canucks have asked for Ben Kindel; no way the Penguins are gonna give up such a promising young player… for a bad contract," Dhaliwal said.

"Teams that are desperate at center call; I checked in this morning, Pettersson has not been asked… to waive his no-move; that tells you… there's nothing close," Dhaliwal added.

Pettersson remains with the Canucks for now despite having been heavily involved in trade rumors over the last several months. While Vancouver traded away the likes of Quinn Hughes, Conor Garland, Tyler Myers, and Kiefer Sherwood last season, Pettersson remained in place.

He still has six years, including the current 2026-27 campaign, left on his contract with an $11.6 million salary cap hit.

Could Elias Pettersson Eventually Land With The Penguins?

The Swedish forward continues to be the subject of trade rumors despite carrying multiple years and a hefty salary cap hit on his contract.

Pettersson, whom the Canucks selected in the first round (fifth overall pick) in the 2017 NHL Draft, has skated in 548 career games and has scored 202 goals with 311 assists. He's also contributed eight goals with 16 assists in 30 games in the Stanley Cup Playoffs.

So far this year, he's tallied twice while adding three assists in three games played.

articles.title: Tobias Harris reveals why he already loves playing alongside Victor Wembanyama
articles.summary: Tobias Harris is already loving his time playing for the Spurs.
articles.body:
Victor Wembanyama has cemented his place among the greatest players in the league today. He has already managed to lead the San Antonio Spurs to the NBA Finals, and he is drawing all kinds of players to help him compete for the championship.

The latest big name to join the Spurs in the latest offseason was Tobias Harris. He went from playing for the #1-seeded Detroit Pistons to possibly the most promising team in the NBA, which just made it to its first NBA Finals as a core group.

Tobias Harris loves what he has seen from Victor Wembanyama up close

Harris has seen and played against Wembanyama before, but now that he's up close, he is getting to see what makes him special behind the scenes. Wembanyama has proven to be one of the league's biggest stars both literally and figuratively.

Defensively, Wembanyama can clean up almost anything with his defensive instincts and his natural size. Offensively, Wembanyama has shown that he can be a dominant player, but he also has some room for improvement.

As a veteran who is also quite an accomplished offensive player, Harris can have a huge impact on Wembanyama's development. Moving forward, it seems that this will be a great addition for the Spurs because they know that Harris provides all types of positive strengths on and off the court.

"He's one of the hardest workers that I've seen in this game. He's such a student of the game, an intelligent player, and very responsive to any type of feedback on the game. Very great to be around; I haven't been around him too long, but I'm looking forward to getting out there and going to battle with him," Harris said about Wembanyama during the Spurs' Media Day .

Moving forward, it will be tough to stop the Spurs because they will have an even better team this time around. They have the experience now, and they are motivated to perform. They even got reinforcements with Harris, so it will be an even more dangerous team to play against, especially with a rejuvanated Wembanyama.

articles.title: La Euroliga se juega su futuro: ocho plazas, 13 aspirantes y 900 millones
articles.standfirst: Asamblea General hoy en el Lago Como para consolidar su expansión y cambiar el mapa del baloncesto europeo alejados por ahora de la sombra de la NBA
articles.summary: Asamblea General hoy en el Lago Como para consolidar su expansión y cambiar el mapa del baloncesto europeo alejados por ahora de la sombra de la NBA
articles.body: La Euroliga sigue adelante con su imparable transición hacia un sistema cerrado de franquicias, proceso que entra en su fase decisiva con la elección de ocho nuevos socios, algo que hará este lunes y martes en la Asamblea General que celebrará en el Lago Como. Allí estarán representados los 13 accionistas dueños de la competición, que decidirán quiénes son los nuevos franquiciados en su proyecto, además de valorar, si es que se produce, alguna oferta de la NBA para unirse a su plan y formar una alianza común. Chus Bueno, CEO de la Euroliga y arquitecto de la nueva competición, comandará la Asamblea y será el que les informe de cualquier novedad que se haya producido al respecto. La emblemática Villa d'Este en Cernobbio, a orillas del Lago de Como, será un bunker blindado donde estarán los dueños y altos ejecutivos de Real Madrid, Barcelona y Baskonia (España); Panathinaikos y Olympiacos (Grecia); Anadolu Efes y Fenerbahçe (Turquía); Armani Milan (Italia); Maccabi Tel Aviv (Israel); Zalgiris Kaunas (Lituania); Bayern Munich (Alemania); ASVEL Villeurbanne (Francia); y CSKA Moscú (Rusia), que serán los que elegirán hasta un máximo de ocho franquiciados (podrían ser menos) entre las 13 candidaturas que ya han superado el primer corte y cuyas ofertas garantizadas en global superan los 900 millones de euros. Valencia Basket, Virtus Bolonia, París Basketball, Hapoel Tel Aviv, Estrella Roja, Partizan, PAOK, Napoli, Dubai Basketball, London Lions y Maxima Roma ya han hecho los deberes y han pasado el primer examen de sus ofertas garantizadas. Y en los últimos días se han sumado el Aris Salónica de Grecia y el Hapoel Jerusalem de Israel. Todos quieren estar. Ahora sus propuestas serán analizadas con lupa por los propietarios de la competición, que tienen una tarea complicada por las altas capacidades que presentan todos los candidatos. La Euroliga no tomarán su decisión basándose sólo en los criterios económicos. Valorará la sostenibilidad a largo plazo de los aspirantes, a los que está sometiendo a una segunda auditoria exhaustiva para verificar la veracidad de sus propuestas y detectar riesgos. Primarán el criterio deportivo, la propiedad, sus recursos, las garantías de estabilidad, su solvencia real, la reputación, la credibilidad institucional y la imagen, el mercado que pueda generar cada candidatura, su masa social, su impacto mediático y el canon de franquicia. Esta es la situación de los 13 equipos que aspiran a convertirse en nuevos franquiciados de la Euroliga, con sus pros y sus contras atendiendo a los requisitos que priorizan los accionistas de la competición y que son los que van a poner en valor antes de determinar cuáles de ellos consideran idóneos para reforzar su proyecto: Son, probablemente, los dos candidatos con más posibilidades de ser aceptados. La razón no es únicamente deportiva. Ambos representan el enorme mercado de Belgrado, tienen una de las mayores aficiones y ambientes de la competición y llevan años siendo considerados por la Euroliga como proyectos estratégicos. De hecho, ambos tienen garantizada su presencia hasta 2027-28 mediante sus actuales licencias de tres años. Presenta varias ventajas que encajan perfectamente con lo que busca la nueva Euroliga: mercado español, una gran instalación con el novísimo Roig Arena, un proyecto económico consolidado, experiencia continuada en Eurocup/Euroliga, capacidad de generar público fuera de toda duda, estabilidad institucional, y una licencia plurianual que ya le fue concedida hasta 2027-28. El Valencia Basket no está luchando simplemente por conservar su actual licencia de tres años. Está intentando dar el salto directamente al nuevo grupo de franquicias permanentes. Y a su favor juega también que la Euroliga no necesita descubrir ni explorar Valencia como mercado. Ya conoce perfectamente su potencial. El único aspecto que podría perjudicarle sería que ya sean tres los clubes españoles en la competición. No es un escollo insalvable. Por tradición, mercado, pabellón, dimensión de la ciudad y peso histórico, la Virtus tiene un perfil muy difícil de rechazar. También dispone de una licencia plurianual hasta 2027-28. Algunos medios de comunicación italianos apuntaron que el conjunto boloñés tendría ya planificada una inversión aproximada de 50 millones de euros a diez años para hacerse con la franquicia de la Euroliga. El París Basketball es otro de los equipos que cuenta con más opciones para ser aceptado. La Euroliga necesita crecer en mercados grandes y París es probablemente el mercado europeo con mayor potencial comercial entre los candidatos. Ya está dentro de la competición y ha demostrado que puede construir una marca internacional relativamente rápido. Por eso, aunque no tenga la tradición de Partizán, Estrella Roja o Virtus, su valor estratégico para la Euroliga es enorme. Dubái aporta unas características que prácticamente ningún otro candidato puede: capital, mercado internacional, capacidad de inversión y proyección hacia Oriente Medio. La Euroliga ya le concedió una licencia de cinco años, hasta 2029-30. Y su pretensión es convertirse en franquicia. Su proyecto ha crecido rápidamente y la Euroliga incluso le otorgó el honor de ser el anfitrión de la nueva Supercopa de la Euroliga. El Hapoel tiene un argumento deportivo muy fuerte: ganó la Eurocup 2024-25 y accedió a la Euroliga por méritos deportivos. Y, además, cuenta con un proyecto económico ambicioso, potenciado por su propietario, el multimillonario Ofer Yannay, obsesionado con convertir a su equipo en uno de los grandes del continente y que no está escatimando recursos para que incluso pueda ser candidato al título. El principal escollo con el que se topa su candidatura, sin ser del todo insalvable, es el contexto geopolítico israelí, una variable negativa que ya le obligó a jugar en el destierro de Sofía (Bulgaria) casi todos sus encuentros como local del pasado curso. Sus opciones para ser aceptado crecerán o menguarán en función de cómo transcurran los acontecimientos. Si no hay una escalada bélica grande por medio tienen muchas opciones de ser elegida. Si la Euroliga quiere convertirse en una competición verdaderamente continental y competir con el proyecto de la NBA Europa, Londres es un mercado extraordinariamente atractivo para potenciar la expansión de la organización. El problema es que el proyecto deportivo de los Lions todavía está muy lejos del peso histórico de los grandes clubes europeos. Pero desde una perspectiva puramente empresarial, Londres puede tener un valor enorme. Si la Euroliga prima mercado, crecimiento y valor comercial, Londres tiene ventaja. Tiene algo que la Euroliga valora mucho: una enorme tradición y una ciudad con cultura de baloncesto. Y ha conseguido pasar el primer corte pese a competir contra proyectos económicamente mucho más potentes. El mercado griego ya está extraordinariamente representado por Olympiacos y Panathinaikos, y la presencia del PAOK podría refrendar aún más su consolidación allí. Si la Euroliga prima tradición, competitividad y solvencia deportiva, PAOK podría entrar en lugar de Londres. El Napoli tiene el atractivo de ser una de las grandes ciudades europeas sin presencia consolidada en la Euroliga y de tener una masa social detrás muy considerable. Pero Italia ya cuenta con Armani Milan y Virtus Bolonia como franquicias/accionistas y ahora Roma intenta entrar. La Euroliga debe estudiar si tiene ya ese mercado suficientemente cubierto o si debería potenciarlo con un franquiciado más. Roma sería el principal rival del Napoli para entrar entre los ocho elegidos, pues tiene probablemente el mercado potencial más grande de los tres italianos candidatos, pero también es el proyecto que genera más interrogantes. La marca Roma es extraordinaria desde el punto de vista comercial, pero la Euroliga necesita comprobar que el proyecto deportivo y financiero tiene la solidez necesaria para mantenerse en la élite. Los griegos de Salónica y el otro Hapoel han sido los últimos en presentar ofertas vinculantes a la Euroliga. El Aris competiría directamente con el PAOK. Y entre los dos israelíes el de Tel Aviv parte con clara ventaja.

articles.title: ENES KANTER FREEDOM: I know the price of silence and won't stop defending women's sports
articles.summary: Enes Kanter Freedom explains how defying Turkey and China over human rights prepared him to speak out on fair competition in women's sports.
articles.body: For most of my life, basketball has been at the center of everything I do. I played 11 seasons in the NBA. I competed against some of the greatest athletes in the world. I know what it takes to reach the highest level of the game — the years of training, the sacrifices, the injuries. But I didn’t become the player I was in front of thousands of people under the bright lights of an NBA arena. I became that player in the hours no one saw. FORMER NBA FIRST ROUND PICK ENES KANTER FREEDOM DECLARES FOR 2027 WNBA DRAFT It happened in empty gyms, one practice at a time. One more shot. One more drill. One more day of showing up and doing the work. The moments that eventually looked big to everyone else were built on thousands of small ones that hardly anyone noticed. I’ve come to believe courage works the same way. We tend to notice courage in the big moments — the speech, the protest, the public stand, the moment someone refuses to back down. But courage is usually built long before anyone is watching. It is built every time you decide that fear will not make your decisions for you. I learned that lesson long before I understood how important it would become in my life. ERDOGAN'S TURKEY CRACKS DOWN ON LGBT COMMUNITY IN NAME OF PRESERVING FAMILY VALUES I grew up in Turkey. When I was a boy, some kids in my neighborhood once handed me an American flag and a lighter and told me to burn it. I spent most of my life competing at the highest levels of basketball. I know what athletes sacrifice for a chance to compete. I didn't understand why I was supposed to hate a country I had never seen or people I had never met. So I went home and asked my mother what I should do. She gave me advice I have never forgotten: "Don't hate anyone before you meet them." It was a small moment. But small moments have a way of shaping a life. Years later, I came to the United States to play basketball. I remember hearing one of my teammates openly criticize the president of the United States. I was shocked. I thought he was crazy. ENES KANTER FREEDOM FILES LAWSUIT AGAINST SKY FOLLOWING EJECTION, BAN AFTER ALTERCATION WITH NATASHA CLOUD Where I came from, criticizing the person in power could carry severe consequences. Here, my teammate laughed and explained something that Americans grow up knowing: This is America. You are allowed to disagree with your government. You are allowed to criticize your leaders. You are allowed to speak. That freedom fascinated me. But eventually, it would still wind up costing me a lot. Speaking up cost me and those I loved enormously. But once you understand what it means to be free, silence comes with a cost of its own. As my basketball career grew, so did my platform. And I began using it to speak about human rights abuses in Turkey and to criticize President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan's government. Of course, I could have stayed quiet, and that would have been much easier and safer. It was a small moment, but I knew it could have an impact. So I spoke. And it was then that I saw the power of one person speaking up. The Turkish government revoked my passport. Arrest warrants were issued for me. My father was imprisoned. My family suffered because of my decisions. I narrowly escaped attempts to detain me abroad. Eventually, the Turkish government placed a $500,000 bounty on my head. Speaking up cost me and those I loved enormously. But once you understand what it means to be free, silence comes with a cost of its own. Later, I began speaking out about the Chinese Communist Party and its treatment of Uyghurs, Tibetans, Hong Kongers and others. I wore shoes onto NBA courts carrying messages the Chinese government did not want displayed. Again, I knew there could be consequences. Again, I spoke anyway. Again, there was a cost. That’s why, when I finally became an American citizen, I chose a new last name: Freedom. I didn't choose it because freedom is an abstract idea to me. I chose it because I know what life looks like when it disappears. Freedom is the ability to ask a question powerful people would rather not answer. It is the right to challenge institutions. It is the right to say something unpopular without surrendering your dignity or your voice. Freedom comes with costs too. This country has seen the cost at which freedom was obtained. Because once you have decided that some principles are worth defending despite enormous consequences, you cannot suddenly decide that other difficult questions are better left alone because people might criticize you. We practice it when people are criticizing us. And perhaps most importantly, we practice it when standing alone would be easier than speaking up. articles.title: La nueva norma de la NBA que cambia el baloncesto de ataque para siempre: así ha sido su impacto

articles.summary: Los árbitros empezarán a sancionar con más severidad a los jugadores que utilicen el brazo para empujar a sus defensores y ganar espacio
articles.body: El primer partido de la pretemporada NBA fue la primera piedra de toque oficial para testar la nueva norma de la NBA que cambiará para siempre la forma de atacar. Con los nuevos criterios los árbitros empezarán a sancionar con más severidad a los jugadores que utilicen el brazo para empujar a sus defensores y ganar espacio. "El objetivo de la liga es garantizar que la forma en que se juega a nuestro baloncesto continúe evolucionando de manera favorable", informaron desde la propia NBA. Para determinar si un empujón con el brazo para ganar espacio es falta en ataque los árbitros deben analiza cuatro conceptos que indican un protocolo muy determinado. "Tenemos que asegurarnos de que el lado defensivo del balón no sea penalizado permitiendo actos ilegales por parte del jugador ofensivo. Habrá algún contacto que consideres afianzamiento y que yo considere con fuerza e ilegal", explicó Monty McCutchen, vicepresidente senior de desarrollo, reconociendo que diferenciar el contacto permitido de la fuerza ilegal representa el mayor desafío de la temporada. En el primer partido de la pretemporada NBA, que enfrentó a los Toronto Raptors con los nuevos Miami Heat de Giannis Antetokounmpo bastaron unos pocos minutos de juego para comprobar la seriedad con la que se toma la NBA este cambio de criterio arbitral. Scottie Barnes fue sancionado con una falta en ataque por empujar a un rival durante los dos primeros minutos del primer cuarto del partido que Toronto perdió ante Miami. 'Sports Illustrated' destaca que "el empujón de Barnes no es flagrante. Sin duda, la temporada pasada no se habría señalado como falta. Pero si ese es el nuevo criterio".

articles.title: Breaking Down Los Angeles Lakers' Projected Rotation for 2026-27 NBA Season
articles.summary: If preseason "vibes" are important, the Los Angeles Lakers are already one of the best teams in the league.
articles.body:
If preseason "vibes" are important, the Los Angeles Lakers are already one of the best teams in the league.

Of course, winning keeps vibes rolling, and it's far from clear how well L.A. stacks up against the talent in the Western Conference.

With LeBron James in Philadelphia with the 76ers and most of the roster turned over since earlier this year, the new-look Lakers should be a fascinating watch—though it's unclear exactly how third-year coach JJ Redick will use the assembled talent.

Redick has remained transparent that two of the team's five starting positions are wide open, as is the bench rotation. Beyond Luka Dončić, Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler, the coach has a long list of players to sort through ahead of the 2026-27 NBA season.

As the franchise kicks off its preseason on Monday in Sacramento against the Kings, we'll get a better sense of what Redick has in mind. In the meantime, here's our best take on what the Lakers' rotation will look like at full strength this upcoming season.

Dončić is among—or outright is—the league's top heliocentric offensive force(s). His combination of size, vision, handling, playmaking, and scoring is currently unparalleled. Dončić has nearly unlimited range on his jump shot and is the player opposing coaches have to scheme against in preparation for the Lakers.

Defense is his greatest weakness, but don't expect Redick to use Dončić as his primary point-of-attack defender. Instead, Quentin Grimes—spoiler—is expected to earn one of the top open starting spots, while defending the opposing team's primary ball-handling guard.

Reaves is a starting-level point guard in his own right, a difficult scoring threat for opponents. Redick will keep Reaves and Dončić on the floor to run the show through most minutes of close games.

Collin Sexton will be the team's primary offensive reserve at point guard, helping satisfy Redick's desire for multiple dribble-pass-shoot threats on the roster. Additional options to round out minutes include Bronny James, Jaden Hardy, and Grimes.

James is an unselfish, serviceable role player and willing defender. Hardy is more of a shooter/scorer, though he insisted on media day that he's here in Los Angeles to defend.

Redick may also utilize players like Ziaire Williams, Matisse Thybulle, Adou Thiero, Jake LaRavia, Jarred Vanderbilt, Cameron Carr, and two-way wing Chris Mañon as point-of-attack defenders when necessary.

Reaves, 6'5", will partner with Dončić, 6'8", in the backcourt, trading off responsibilities depending on opponents' schemes. They represent the Lakers' primary offensive attack, stacking up favorably against any team in the league—on offense.

The reserve list is long, including Grimes, Sexton, Hardy, Carr, Thybulle, Williams, James, Thiero, LaRavia, Vanderbilt, and Dalton Knecht. The Lakers have 16 players under standard contracts, one more than allowed for the regular season; Knecht appears to be the odd man out at this early stage.

Grimes, Sexton, and Hardy represent scoring options—as does Carr, though it's difficult to project that the rookie will earn regular minutes early in the season. Otherwise, Redick wanted a squad of defensive options to plug in, helping to complement/offset the two backcourt stars.

Grimes' $14 million salary for 2026-27, the fourth-highest on the team, suggests he'll be in the starting group with Dončić, Reaves and Kessler.

Redick hasn't shied away from three-guard lineups, regularly relying on Marcus Smart last season to take on the toughest perimeter assignments.

Grimes, 6'5", spent the first three years of his career with defensive-minded former New York Knicks coach Tom Thibodeau in a similar role.

Grimes is also a capable scorer, averaging 21.9 points over a 28-game stretch after his trade from the Dallas Mavericks to the Philadelphia 76ers in 2025. The same cast of characters can back him up, including Williams, Thybulle, Thiero, Vanderbilt, Carr, Mañon, and Knecht (if still on the roster).

Dončić and Reaves are also options throughout the rotation. Redick has options, and he's made it clear to his players that the ones who excel defensively will play.

Salary doesn't always indicate a player's role in the team's hierarchy. Sandro Mamukelashvili was one of the Lakers' top targets this summer, signing a four-year $52 million deal. Still, his value as a big, offensive connector may be best served coming off the bench.

Mamukelashvili will finish the year among the top five in minutes, but Williams is the stronger fit in a Jaden McDaniels starting role. Listed at 185 pounds, Williams recently indicated he's closer to 215.

At just 25, Williams has a real opportunity to establish himself as a vital starter, despite his minimum contract. His positional flexibility on defense and potential as a catch-and-shoot floor spacer could be the perfect fit alongside Dončić and Reaves.

That would slot Mamukelashvili as the team's sixth man, playing heavy minutes at power forward and center. LaRavia, Vanderbilt and Thiero will also get time at the four. Kevon Looney brings a wealth of experience and knowledge, and while he projects to play more behind Kessler, Redick may also find use for him at forward.

The Lakers need Williams, Mamukelashvili and their current depth to step up, as the starting power forward spot is the biggest rotational question mark.

The Lakers gave up most of their remaining draft capital to acquire Kessler from the Utah Jazz. He's an imposing defensive rim protector, but that will only help if the perimeter players can stay in front of their assignments.

Kessler was a force in Utah, but the team was among the league's worst on defense.

And the Lakers—coaching staff and players—get it. They understand what it will take to build a viable defense around Kessler and the flaws inherent in a Dončić/Reaves backcourt. Whether they can execute their vision is a different topic entirely, but it should be entertaining to watch as L.A. tries to figure it out through the highs and lows.

Depth behind Kessler is thin, with Mamukelashvili as a viable offensive option and Looney a capable defensive reserve. Neither is suitable for an extended stretch should Kessler miss significant time.

The Lakers appear to be one reliable backup center short of a complete rotation—ideally one capable of handling roughly 18 minutes per game—but they could address that need before February's trade deadline.

In the meantime, the Lakers have a clear plan for approaching the 2026-27 campaign. Redick's rotation remains a work in progress, but it will rely heavily on Williams thriving at power forward and a deep wing group complementing the Lakers' top three players.

If the Lakers stay healthy, they should contend for a No. 5 or No. 6 seed in the Western Conference. Their ceiling is higher, but their floor is lower if the roster's pieces do not fit together as well as the front office anticipates.

articles.title: NBA Trade Idea to Give Golden State Warriors an Alternative All-Star Upgrade
articles.summary: After spending so much of Stephen Curry's tenure in the NBA's elite tier, the Golden State Warriors have backtracked into the league's dreaded midsection.
articles.body:
After spending so much of Stephen Curry's tenure in the NBA's elite tier, the Golden State Warriors have backtracked into the league's dreaded midsection.

Even worse, there's no obvious way for them to snap out of it. While the Warriors clearly need more help around Curry to have any shot at winning something of substance, the risk-reward calculations of an all-in type of trade seldom return encouraging results.

Golden State clearly won't make a move for the sake of doing a deal, and it seemingly has understandable questions about just how far a significant trade can take it. Especially since most star swaps would, for money-matching purposes, require the subtraction of a key component (like Jimmy Butler or Draymond Green).

But what if the Warriors could find an alternate path to an All-Star upgrade? Because there is a certain 2025-26 All-Star who might be a trade chip as soon as he is trade-eligible, doesn't have the kind of sky-high salary that would necessitate one of those aforementioned cuts to this core and should be gettable for far less than Golden State's full allotment of trade assets.

Sounds intriguing, right? Well, let's fire up the trade machine and get this (hypothetical) deal done.

Golden State Warriors receive: Norman Powell (trade-eligible on Dec. 15) and Jalen Smith

Chicago Bulls receive: Kristaps Porziņģis, Moses Moody, Brandin Podziemski and a 2028 1st-round pick (top-4 protected)

External expectations are nonexistent for this team, but internally Curry still feels an "absolute desperation to win," as the four-time champion told ESPN's Anthony Slater .

The Warriors would presumably love to give him some kind of shot at winning—they'd just prefer to do so without mortgaging their very uncertain future without him.

This could be the perfect have-their-cake-and-eat-it compromise. Curry would get plenty of offensive support from Powell, whose late-career ascension has seen him average 20-plus points in consecutive seasons and earn an All-Star nod in the most recent one, while Golden State would be out only one (near-) future first.

This deal wouldn't force the Dubs to fork over Draymond Green, still a mission-critical component of the system, or Jimmy Butler, a two-way star (when healthy, obviously) who helped Curry and this club reach the 2025 conference semis. It also wouldn't ship out draft picks that would convey after Curry finished his tenure with the team.

A Curry-Powell-Butler-Green quartet feels like the kind of experienced, savvy combo no club would want to draw come playoff time. Golden State was far from good last season, but the Warriors played like a top-five team ( plus-6.9 net rating, would've ranked fifth overall ) when Curry, Butler and Green shared the floor.

Add in Powell, who would bring championship experience, perimeter sharpshooting (a 39.6 percent career three-point shooter) and the downhill scoring element this offense often lacks.

Yaxel Lendeborg—a leading scorer and stat-sheet stuffer for Michigan's NCAA championship team—could add another dimension. If the rookie lottery pick proves to be a capable spacer at the NBA level, those pieces could align in intriguing fashion.

The Dubs should still have sufficient depth. De'Anthony Melton and Brandon Williams could split Podziemski's vacated minutes. Lendeborg, Gui Santos and Will Richard would cover Moses Moody's absence on the wing as he works his way back from a serious knee injury.

Golden State would even have a shot-blocking, floor-spacing replacement for Porziņģis with Smith, who might be far less dynamic but is also far more reliable.

It's the kind of group that could give Curry hope while, again, avoiding a gutting of Golden State's asset base.

Bulls fans who had waited years for this inevitable rebuild must have their imaginations running wild over what the future might hold for young forwards Caleb Wilson and Matas Buzelis.

But shouldn't there be more to look forward to? Especially when the short-term outlook appears so rough ?

Even if Chicago sees building-block potential in all three of Josh Giddey, Noa Essengue and Dailyn Swain—and there are reasons to question each one—that's still a pretty shallow young core for a rebuilder.

This deal might go a long way toward deepening it. Podziemski, 23, has already popped as a complementary scorer, shooter and creator with flashes of becoming even more. Moody, 24, is a willing and able wing defender who made better than 40 percent from three on better than six attempts a night last season.

Throw in that future first—plus Porziņģis as a money-matcher with little guaranteed beyond this season—and this feels like the exact kind of package Chicago was hoping to get back when it surprisingly signed Powell, whose timeline misaligns with this team's by a mile.

If the Bulls guessed right on Podziemski as a long-term keeper, they might already have the backcourt component needed to complement their frontcourt. There are, admittedly, loads of defensive concerns with a Giddey-Podziemski guard tandem, but their combined scoring potency and playmaking capabilities could simplify quite a bit for Wilson and Buzelis.

Now, that could realistically comprise 80 percent of a long-term starting five, and Chicago would still have Swain, Essengue and Moody on the second unit. That reads a lot more like a rebuilder's young nucleus, and that's before factoring in whatever the Bulls might find in their upcoming drafts.

And who knows, maybe Chicago could get really lucky and have Porziņģis heal up in time to emerge as a deadline target for a desperate shopper? That would only add to what already feels like a strong haul for a 33-year-old one-time All-Star and a 26-year-old backup big.

articles.title: 'Played Like Ass,' Becky Hammon Video of Honest Quote Goes Viral After Aces' Loss to Valkyries
articles.summary: Las Vegas Aces coach Becky Hammon had a blunt assessment of her team's performance in a 71-60 loss to the Golden State Valkyries.
articles.body:
Las Vegas Aces coach Becky Hammon had a blunt assessment of her team's performance in a 71-60 loss to the Golden State Valkyries.

Hammon tried to find a silver lining by suggesting the Aces "played like ass and only lost by [11]."

The Valkyries were the WNBA's best defensive team in the regular season and showed why to open their semifinal series. Las Vegas' Big Three of A'ja Wilson, Chelsea Gray and Jackie Young combined to shoot 17-of-50 (34 percent) from the field. In the case of Wilson, it was just the sixth time all year she was under 40 percent.

Golden State also had 52 rebounds, including 17 on the offensive glass, to 25 for the Aces.

"All we talked about for the last 48 hours was rebounding and blocking them out, and we did not do it. Period," Hammon told reporters .

Valkyries center Kiah Stokes went scoreless yet still had one of the biggest impacts of anybody on the floor. She hauled in 14 boards and blocked four shots as she helped neutralize Wilson.

Golden State coach Natalie Nakase called her the game's MVP.

"Her disruption, her matching up with A'ja, it's a really tough task," Nakase said . "She did an amazing job, just continue to keep her off rhythm as much as we can. … Kiah was vicious on the boards, her ability I thought today was emptying that tank. That's the Kiah Stokes we know. For sure, she made the difference today."

Any playoff series is about making adjustments. The Valkyries had a winning plan for Game 1. Now, the onus is on the Aces to adapt and get the trio of Wilson, Gray and Young back to their best.

The semifinals will resume Wednesday, so having two days off should benefit both the Vegas players and coaching staff.

articles.title: Kenny Atkinson backs NBA Europe as Cleveland Cavaliers coach praises European player 'mentoring'
articles.summary: Cavaliers coach backs the NBA's planned European league and praises how club systems put teenagers against men in a way the US college game never will; NBA targets London and Manchester for franchises in league set to launch in October 2027
articles.body:
The Cleveland Cavaliers head coach, the reigning NBA Coach of the Year, was speaking at the end of his team's training camp in Malaga last week. He spent most of a decade playing in Europe and began his coaching career there.

Atkinson said: "I love the NBA. I love that we are in talks with FIBA to create this NBA Europe. It's going to bring more opportunity for players across the globe."

Asked what European players arrive with that the American system does not produce, he pointed to how the two systems are built.

"The European system is a club system and we just don't work that way," Atkinson told Sky Sports. "We have the university system, the scholastic system, and it's just different."

"They might be playing for the under-16 team or under-17, but they also train with the older guys. Or like in France, the INSEP team, the young team, they play in the third division of France, so they're getting to compete against older players. I think that mentoring system is really important."

He was explicit about where the American model differs from the European one.

Atkinson said: "In the American system we're much more playing against your peers and at the same age, and our young players don't compete against more mature players as much. You learn a lot from veteran players."

"But they both have their benefits. It's hard to say this one's better than this one. Definitely two completely different ways of developing players."

The detail he cited holds up. The INSEP side, entered by the French federation as Pole France, plays in Nationale 1, the third tier of French men's basketball. Its squad last season ran from 15 to 18 years old, and it can be neither promoted nor relegated.

Atkinson knows the ground better than most Americans in his job. He played at Montpellier, Mulhouse, Nantes and Evreux in France, with spells in Spain and Germany, and began coaching as an assistant at Paris Basket Racing in 2004. He was on Vincent Collet's staff when France took Olympic silver in Paris.

Asked whether a European league might bring the two systems closer together, he said: "I love that. I think it's going to be better for global basketball, because that cross-pollination, you're going to see the best of both worlds."

"You already see in the coaching world the mix of the European influence on the NBA, right? FIBA influence. And I think vice versa, the NBA has influenced Europe, so we have that in the coaching community. It'll be great to see it with the players too."

Atkinson has an example of the European model on his own roster.

Khalifa Diop was playing in Spain's fourth tier at 15 and in the ACB at 19. Cleveland drafted him 39th in 2022 and left him in Spain for four more years before signing him last month.

The NBA and FIBA have been jointly exploring a new pan-European league since March 2025. The NBA's plan is for a league comprised of 16 teams, 12 permanent franchises and four annual qualifiers, launching in the autumn of 2027, with target cities that include London and Manchester.

New Orleans play San Antonio at Co-op Live on Sunday January 17, the first NBA regular-season game staged in Manchester.

Merrill: NBA Europe would have been a great option

The idea already has an audience among players.

Cavaliers guard Sam Merrill, asked the previous day whether a European league would have been a realistic option for him coming out of Utah State, said it would have been.

"I had a point in my career where I felt like I was going to end up coming overseas," he said. "And if that had been the case, something like NBA Europe would have been a great option."

Merrill went 60th in the 2020 draft, the last pick, and spent two years in the G League before Cleveland signed him. He has been following the project as it takes shape.

He also raised an important point in terms of the finances associated with the respective pathways.

Merrill said: "You got all these guys making so much money in college now. I'm interested to see how that conflicts with NBA Europe."

Since July 2025 American universities have paid their players directly. The cap for 2026-27 is $21.58m a school, with men's basketball programmes averaging around $4.2m of it, and Forbes reported last month that a power-conference roster now costs $7m to $10m a season.

Since then the traffic has run one way. Egor Demin left Real Madrid for BYU and Dame Sarr left Barcelona for Duke. Whether a new league changes that depends on money nobody has yet put a number on. Sportico reported bids for NBA Europe franchises within and beyond the $500m to $1bn range but neither the NBA nor FIBA has said anything about what the league would pay the players it hopes to keep.

Merrill, for his part, has watched the European game closely from a distance.

"I love the physicality of the leagues over here," he said. "It's much more college-like, where you have your two games a week, and you practice a lot more, and every game feels almost much more important, kind of like a playoff game."

"I think people underrate how good, especially EuroLeague and the top leagues domestically, how good those things are."

EuroLeague summit set to shape Europe's next move

The next move belongs to the clubs. EuroLeague shareholders meet at Villa d'Este in Cernobbio, on Lake Como, on Monday, with the competition's own future on the table alongside the NBA's interest in it.

La Gazzetta dello Sport reported last month that the assembly would weigh a proposal from the NBA against the EuroLeague's own expansion plans. No agenda has been published and the EuroLeague has made no statement on the meeting.

The two routes are to evaluate an NBA proposal to acquire the EuroLeague and fold it into the new competition, or to press ahead with chief executive Chus Bueno's own plan to expand to 24 teams, with 21 permanent franchises, from 2027-28. Eight new franchises are expected to be named.

Bueno told The Athletic in September that nothing had yet arrived. "As of today, we have not received anything from the NBA about what a potential partnership or collaboration could look like."

Since then, though, Eurohoops has reported that an offer was on the table, although both the NBA and the EuroLeague declined to comment.

Adam Silver has said the NBA will proceed either way. "We began on this path saying that our plan was to go forward regardless of where the EuroLeague stood," he said, back in July.

"But it was always our hope that we would be able to create some sort of consolidation of European basketball. I remain optimistic that we are going to be able to accomplish that."
