articles.title: Mike Conley Already Showing Why the Celtics Signed Him
articles.summary: The veteran point guard is earning rave reviews from his new teammates and coach.
articles.body:
Mike Conley is already making his presence felt on the Boston Celtics .

Shortly after the Celtics signed Conley, president of basketball operations Brad Stevens gushed about the 19-year NBA veteran's leadership and ability to impact winning.

We'll have to wait and see how much gas he has left in the tank, but Conley's leadership is already on full display.

"I think he's won the teammate awards because of the kind of person he is, and like, just reliable and just a good dude and somebody you can always talk to and lean on," Payton Pritchard said about Conley . "But for me, somebody that looked up to Mike, it's like how he thinks of the game and how he was able to create his shots and create shots for his teammates, and maybe handle playing the point guard position, momentum swings.

"You know, he's been in a lot of great environments, great playoff series, and like how was he able to kill in those moments and dominate the game."

The 2026-27 season will mark Conley's 20th NBA season. He joins the Celtics as a one-time All-Star with one All-Defensive team selection. He's never won an NBA championship, but he's played a key role in deep playoff runs with the Memphis Grizzlies, Utah Jazz and Minnesota Timberwolves.

Additionally, Conley has won the NBA's Sportsmanship Award four times in his career. That's the most in NBA history, and he's one of only five players to win the award multiple times.

That reputation as a respected teammate appears to have followed him to Boston.

Pritchard isn't the only one who has spoken highly of Conley at training camp. Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla also revealed how his leadership is making a difference.

"Leadership just comes naturally to him, and I think people flock to him in general as being a great teammate," Mazzulla said . "I think it's really just his personality. You know, like I said, leadership becomes very natural to him. He's constantly coming into the building worrying about others and not worrying about himself, which I think says a lot about him, but also the experience of you know of what he's been in, and he comes in very present."

The Celtics signed Conley to a one-year, $3.9 million contract in the offseason. He's already making an impact before playing a regular-season game for the Celtics.

articles.title: LeBron James has two injuries the 76ers are already treating
articles.summary: A lot of concern surrounds LeBron James as the 76ers are already treating two scary injuries before the 2026-27 NBA season.
articles.body:
Father Time has always been undefeated in the NBA. Regardless of how long a career is, age and fatigue will always come to haunt a player. LeBron James has avoided both for a long time. However, something seems different as he enters the 2026-27 NBA season. What seems to be the problem? Well, the Philadelphia 76ers are already taking precautions because of two concerning injuries that have surfaced before the start of their regular season.

76ers unveil two concerning LeBron James injuries before NBA season start

Injuries rarely keep LeBron James out of games. He has gone on to go on the court during nights when excruciating pain ran amok in his body. This has become more prevalent in recent years. He has been sidelined more often for load management and to avoid fatigue. On some nights, some injuries have also just been too much for James to play through; that's why he gets deactivated from the rotation.

All of these usually happen in the middle of the season. Typically, James is ready to go when the season starts. However, this time it might be different as he enters his first stint with the 76ers. Why is that? It seems he's already being treated for two injuries heading into the 76ers' 2026-27 82-game campaign, per Dave McMenamin of ESPN.

"And there is special attention paid to his left foot, which has chronic arthritis, sources told ESPN, and his lower back, which caused him to miss the first month of last season because of sciatica," the NBA insider declared.

Notably, this foot injury has been recurring for James. During his time with the Los Angeles Lakers , he already missed time to deal with this pain. In fact, this is the most recurring pain that he has been treating in the past year. James had to sit out certain games during November, January, February, and April. This will clearly keep him out of Coach Nick Nurse's system for a bit during the 2026-27 NBA season.

Moreover, this reported lower back pain is also nothing new for James. His sciatica has also been a recurring problem that the 76ers have to deal with. In his 2025-26 run with the Lakers, James couldn't play because of the same pain in October, November, and December.

This raises a lot of questions. First, retirement is likely nearing for James, as these chronic pains probably won't slow down if he keeps playing. It also probably means he will be in and out of Coach Nick Nurse's rotation to manage his fatigue. As a result, Jaylen Brown will be the main forward and the 76ers' offensive focal point.

Keeping James healthy will be one of the main keys to the 76ers' title contention hopes. Sure, he brings a great deal of intangibles, but it's different to see him orchestrate an offense or wreck opponents with advanced defensive schemes.

articles.title: WNBA clears A’ja Wilson of further punishment after courtside confrontation
articles.summary: Keeton Gale/Shutterstock.com A’ja Wilson receives no further punishment Las Vegas Aces star A’ja Wilson received no additional WNBA discipline after confront...
articles.body:
A'ja Wilson receives no further punishment

Las Vegas Aces star A'ja Wilson received no additional WNBA discipline after confronting a courtside fan during Game 2 against the Indiana Fever on September 29, 2026, at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in Indianapolis.

The league declined to fine or suspend Wilson after determining she remained inside the designated player escape lane. Officials had already assessed a technical foul for unsportsmanlike conduct during the fourth quarter.

The confrontation began with 4:10 remaining in the fourth quarter after Sophie Cunningham was called for a foul involving Wilson. Indiana led 90-79 when a nearby fan stood and pointed toward Wilson.

Wilson walked toward the baseline seating area, pointed back, and exchanged words with the fan. Teammates, an assistant coach, and security personnel intervened before play resumed inside Gainbridge Fieldhouse that evening.

Officials assessed Wilson a technical foul for unsportsmanlike conduct during the confrontation. She remained in the game after officials determined she was in the player escape lane rather than the spectator stands.

That location mattered because deliberately entering spectator stands can trigger automatic ejection. The WNBA later imposed no fine or suspension, leaving the technical foul as Wilson's only formal penalty from the incident.

Arena security temporarily escorted the fan away from the courtside area following the confrontation. Indiana reviewed the incident to determine whether the spectator had violated the arena's Fan Code of Conduct.

The fan was allowed to return after security found no violation of the Fan Code of Conduct. That arena decision remained separate from the WNBA disciplinary review of Wilson and other Las Vegas players.

Wilson said after Game 2 that the fan stepped toward her and pointed at her. She described that behavior as unacceptable and apologized to her Las Vegas teammates for receiving the technical foul.

Wilson said the specific words or tone did not change her objection to the fan's actions. She emphasized the movement toward her and the pointing while accepting responsibility for the technical foul.

Head coach Becky Hammon defended Wilson's reaction after Game 2, saying she had rarely seen Wilson respond so strongly. Hammon said the response showed Wilson felt deeply disrespected by the courtside interaction.

Hammon has coached Wilson in Las Vegas since 2022 and emphasized how unusual the reaction was for her star player. Her comments did not change the technical foul or subsequent league review.

Indiana won Game 2 by 99-89, evening the opening first-round series at 1-1. Wilson finished with 22 points and nine rebounds, while Jackie Young led Las Vegas with 31 points.

The loss forced a deciding Game 3 in Las Vegas. Wilson received no additional discipline and remained eligible to play in the elimination game at Michelob ULTRA Arena on October 1.

A'ja Wilson scores 36 in deciding Game 3

Wilson scored 36 points and collected 10 rebounds in Game 3 as Las Vegas defeated Indiana 94-83. The Aces won the series 2-1 and advanced to the WNBA semifinal round.

Wilson made 11 of 18 field goal attempts and added two blocked shots in the deciding victory. The performance came two days after the courtside confrontation and ended Indiana's 2026 postseason run.

A'ja Wilson enters playoffs as scoring leader

Las Vegas entered the postseason as the No. 3 seed after finishing the regular season 31-13. Wilson averaged 26.2 points per game and led the WNBA in scoring for a third consecutive season.

Wilson also received 15 of 17 first-place votes for the 2026 Associated Press WNBA Player of the Year award. The honor marked her third consecutive selection by that panel.

A'ja Wilson entered series with four MVPs

Wilson entered the series as a four-time WNBA MVP. The league's review of the Game 2 confrontation resulted in no additional fine, suspension, or other disciplinary action against the Las Vegas star.

Wilson played all three games of the first-round series and remained available for the deciding Game 3. She scored 36 points as Las Vegas defeated Indiana and advanced to the semifinals.

Fun fact: Wilson became the first WNBA player ever to score 1,000 points in one regular season, finishing 2024 with 1,021. That is a lot of buckets.

Kalani Brown and Kierstan Bell avoid discipline

Las Vegas reserves Kalani Brown and Kierstan Bell left the bench area during the confrontation. The WNBA also decided not to impose additional discipline on either player after reviewing the incident.

Brown and Bell remained available for the deciding Game 3, as did Wilson. The league's decision resolved the disciplinary status of all three Las Vegas players before the October 1 game.

Indiana player Sophie Cunningham later criticized the WNBA's decision and publicly argued that Wilson received favorable treatment. Cunningham's comments represented her own view, while the league's disciplinary ruling remained unchanged.

Cunningham's criticism did not affect Wilson's eligibility. Wilson played Game 3 as scheduled, scored 36 points, and helped Las Vegas advance, making the no suspension decision a completed disciplinary matter.

LeBron James' next chapter marks a major shift in the NBA landscape. Check out what convinced LeBron James to leave the Lakers for Philadelphia?

Wilson opened the first-round series with 38 points and 16 rebounds in a 102-85 Las Vegas victory. She scored 22 points in Game 2 before adding 36 in the deciding Game 3.

Las Vegas advanced after defeating Indiana 2-1 in the series. Golden State then defeated the Aces 71-60 in Game 1 of their best-of-five semifinal on October 4 at Chase Center. Wilson led Las Vegas with 24 points, and Game 2 is scheduled for October 7 at Chase Center.

Wondering how the Aces have handled other high-profile moments? Explore Candace Parker's blunt on-air criticism of Caitlin Clark during their matchup.

As Philadelphia 76ers star forward LeBron James prepares to enter his 24th NBA season, he continues to try to make sure his body is prepared for the grind of a full season.

According to ESPN's Dave McMenamin , James' left foot and lower back get "special attention" after the injuries have been an issue in the past:

"And there is special attention paid to his left foot, which has chronic arthritis, sources told ESPN, and his lower back, which caused him to miss the first month of last season because of sciatica."

James was limited to 60 games in his last season with the Los Angeles Lakers in 2025-26, missing the first 14 games due to his lower back. It was his fourth time in the last six seasons playing in fewer than 65 games.

It was revealed late last month that James will be using a helicopter to commute between Philadelphia and New York—where he will live—during the season.

Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said at the start of training camp that the team has had discussions about managing the workloads of James and star center Joel Embiid during the regular season. The team intended to figure out a plan for back-to-backs.

Despite the injuries, James averaged 20.9 points, 6.1 rebounds, 7.2 assists and 1.2 steals in 2025-26 as he helped lead the Lakers to the Western Conference Semifinals.

After becoming a free agent, James joined a star-studded Sixers team that has a core including Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe and Jaylen Brown, the latter of whom was acquired in an offseason trade with the Boston Celtics.

The Sixers will be focused on chasing an NBA championship, so they will be sure not to overwork the legend at this stage of his career.

articles.summary: According to NBA reporter Marc Stein, Golden State Warriors guard Brandin Podziemski is one of the likely candidates for a contract extension this week, joining the likes of Brandon Miller in Charlotte, Anthony Black in Orlando) and Cason Wallace in Oklahoma City.
articles.body:
According to NBA reporter Marc Stein , Golden State Warriors guard Brandin Podziemski is one of the likely candidates for a contract extension this week, joining the likes of Brandon Miller in Charlotte, Anthony Black in Orlando) and Cason Wallace in Oklahoma City.

Per that report, "Regarding Podziemski specifically: Word relayed to The Stein Line this week is that both sides want to get a deal done... but that is obviously dependent on beating the ticking clock."

The deadline to sign rookie scale extensions is Monday, Oct. 19.

San Antonio's Victor Wembanyama, Houston's Amen Thompson, Detroit's Ausar Thompson and Utah's Keyonte George are the only players from the 2023 draft class to sign rookie-scale extensions thus far.

Podziemski, 23, averaged 13.8 points, 5.1 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 1.1 steals per game last season across 82 appearances (43 starts), shooting 45.5 percent from the field and 37.1 percent from three. He was a different player after the All-Star break, however, averaging 17.5 points across 27 contests.

That's the version the Warriors want to see going forward.

"From talking to Steve [Kerr], talking to [general manager[ Mike [Dunleavy], end-of-season meetings, they're kinda just like, 'Do what you were doing the last six weeks,'" Podziemski told Luca Evans of the San Francisco Chronicle . "And so, I know I have confidence from them and my teammates to do the same things. And now it's about like, where are the little gaps to add a little bit more than what I was doing?"

Thus far he's had a strong training camp, with Kerr going so far as to describe it as "great" last week through the first three days.

"That's what we like about Brandin: His ability to see the game, attack angles and he understands the officiating," Kerr told reporters. "He can dribble, pass, shoot. You can put him at any spot out of a timeout. Really versatile and obviously crucial to make the whole thing go."

As for whether that translates to a lucrative extension remains to be seen.

"I mean, obviously, I would love a deal," Podz told Evans. "I think at the moment, all options are on the table. Obviously, there's been mutual interest between me and the organization, and so if we're able to get something done, that'd be beautiful. But like I said, all options are always on the table, until it's a done deal."

articles.title: Karl-Anthony Towns' Rumored Contract Offer Revealed After Knicks Star Says Deal Isn't 'Close'
articles.summary: New York Knicks star Karl-Anthony Towns all but confirmed an earlier report that contract negotiations between he and the team haven't progressed much, with details of the team's offer also surfacing.
articles.body:
New York Knicks star Karl-Anthony Towns all but confirmed an earlier report that contract negotiations between he and the team haven't progressed much, with details of the team's offer also surfacing.

Stefan Bondy of the New York Post reported that the Knicks have offered a contract around $200 million, which would be $77 million below a max deal.

That news comes after Towns outlined what he wants on his new deal and said "none of those things are close to happening." When asked if he thought it'd be easy to get a deal done after a championship run, Towns responded (via ESPN ), "No s--t, Sherlock. I just won a championship. You'd think it was pretty easy. Unless you guys think I have something else to prove."

NBA Players with the All-Time Most Career Earnings💰

The six-time All-Star has a $61 million player option for 2027-28. He'll presumably decline that in pursuit of a far bigger overall payout.

Towns can re-sign for up to $276 million over four years with the Knicks. The Athletic's James L. Edwards III reported on Sept. 23 that New York won't put a full max on the table. In addition, the respective parties "are far enough apart now" that a resolution could drag into the regular season.

According to Stefan Bondy of the New York Post , the team is prepared to pay "around $200 million" on a four-year deal.

Knicks star Jalen Brunson left a significant amount of money on the table when he signed a four-year, $156.5 million extension. That was intended to give the front office more salary cap flexibility and perhaps entice others to take less than the max.

On the heels of New York's NBA Finals triumph, the priorities for those on the roster may have shifted a bit. Towns, for example, captured the title that serves as validation after people questioned his role on a team with championship aspirations.

"I've made it known I want to play here," KAT said during the Knicks' media day. "I've been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done and step on the floor and feel as comfortable as possible."

But the 30-year-old also knows his value may never be higher than it will be in 2027. His remarks from Monday are certainly telling.

The Knicks, meanwhile, have to bake another Brunson extension into their financial projections for the future.

"Obviously we'd love for them to do right by me," he told Tom Kludt of Vanity Fair for a story published this past February. "I think anyone would. I feel like I sacrificed."

The Athletic's Fred Katz reported last week that "all signs point to the NBA Finals MVP earning a significant raise — a projected $290 million over four years." Having his average salary climb from $39.1 million to more than $70 million would have massive consequences for the Knicks.

That's why negotiations with Towns have been and may continue to be tense. Assuming Brunson will pocket the max or something close to it in a few years, Knicks president Leon Rose will need to be very purposeful with the budget with that in mind.

articles.title: Alex Ovechkin announces 2026-27 Capitals campaign will be final season of NHL career
articles.summary: No one has scored more regular-season goals in NHL history than Ovechkin.
articles.body:
Washington Capitals icon Alex Ovechkin, the NHL's all-time leading scorer, has announced that the 2026-27 campaign will be the final season of his prolific career.

"My family and I decided this summer that this will be my final year in the NHL," Ovechkin, 41, said in a statement the Capitals released on Monday . "I love this game so much, but I know in my heart it's the right decision. It was important for me to make this announcement before our first home game, so I have the chance to thank all the people around the game, everyone who has been so important to me and my family and helped me through good times and tough losses. I wouldn't have been able to achieve everything I have in my life without them. "I am excited about this season with my teammates, and we will do everything we can to make this year special. I am going to enjoy every moment with my family, my boys, our fans and everyone who has been part of my hockey career." Ovechkin added, alluding to the Capitals' Wednesday night home opener against the Pittsburgh Penguins: "See you Wednesday, babes!"

Ovechkin added, alluding to the Capitals' Wednesday night home opener against the Pittsburgh Penguins: "See you Wednesday, babes!"

The Capitals also posted a message Ovechkin shared with the team Monday morning.

He told his teammates in person that this is going to be his last season in the league.

"For me, for my family, it's very important that you guys know first," Ovechkin said . "And yeah, it's sad, but it is what it is. … Let's make the playoffs, let's have fun and enjoy the moment because times fly. "For young guys who [it's your] first year, or experienced guys, remember that moment and enjoy the time because of how I said times fly. It seems like yesterday I was here my first year, and right now this is my 22nd year, and it just goes like this." Ovechkin snapped his fingers and then concluded: "So yeah, it's hard, but let's enjoy it, and let's do some special things this year."

Ovechkin snapped his fingers and then concluded: "So yeah, it's hard, but let's enjoy it, and let's do some special things this year."

The beloved Russian superstar, affectionately nicknamed "Ovi," was then met with a standing ovation in the locker room.

Ovechkin will wrap his NHL career with 22 seasons played, all with the Capitals. After this go-around, he will hang up his skates and put the bow on a record-filled NHL career — one that will undoubtedly see him earn entrance into the Hockey Hall of Fame when he is first eligible.

The top record Ovechkin holds is total NHL goals scored , which he set in April 2025 with his 895th tally to break a tie with Wayne Gretzky . Since, he's added 34 more goals to increase that total to 929.

Ovechkin put NHL goaltenders on alert beginning with his first season in 2005-06, when he scored 52 times — the first of nine times he's reached the 50-goal mark in his career. His regular-season goals have helped him earn nine Maurice "Rocket" Richard Trophies as the league's top goal scorer.

Ovechkin, the No. 1 overall pick by the Capitals in the 2004 NHL Draft, also holds the record of most 40-goal seasons with 14 and is tied with Gretzky and Mike Bossy with nine 50-goal seasons.

Goal-related marks haven't been the only accomplishments in Ovechkin's career. He was the 2005-06 Calder Memorial Trophy winner as rookie of the year, and he's won one Art Ross Trophy as the league's top point-getter, earned eight NHL First-Team All-Star honors and appeared in nine NHL All-Star Games, in addition to becoming a three-time Hart Memorial Trophy winner as league MVP.

In 2017, Ovechkin was named one of the 100 greatest NHL players of all time .

For the first decade-plus of his NHL career, while Ovechkin scored consistently, one thing was missing: a Stanley Cup title.

After failing to advance past the second round of the Stanley Cup Playoffs since 1998, the Capitals exorcised their postseason demons by not only beating the Penguins for the first time in nine series but also winning the first championship in franchise history in 2018.

Ovechkin was voted Conn Smythe Trophy winner as playoff MVP after scoring 15 goals and recording 27 points in 24 games for the Capitals that postseason. He would celebrate accordingly that summer.

While the Capitals have yet to match that postseason success, Ovechkin continued his goal-scoring exploits. Over the next eight seasons, he notched two 50-goal and three 40-goal campaigns.

One accomplishment that has eluded Ovechkin has been an Olympic gold medal. Russia failed to medal in the three tournaments he was a part of, including 2014 in Sochi. He found other success internationally, though, with three gold medals at the World Championship and World Junior Championship gold in 2003, one year before he was drafted by the Capitals.

Ovechkin's résumé is long, and his impact on the game of hockey and the NHL is immeasurable. His influence on the game can be seen in the skill sets of today's younger players. The Hall of Fame will be there for him three years after the 2026-27 season ends, unless the Hall decides to (rightly) make an exception and allow early entry, as it did for the likes of Gretzky, Mario Lemieux and Bobby Orr, among others.

articles.title: How can Aces and Liberty, WNBA's most recent champions, bounce back after semifinal Game 1 losses?
articles.summary: Firepower offenses took their star turn in the regular season. Now it's the defenses standing strongest to start the WNBA semifinals.
articles.body:
ATLANTA — Firepower offenses took their star turn in the regular season. Now it's the defenses standing strongest to start the WNBA semifinals .

The No. 2 Golden State Valkyries and No. 4 Atlanta Dream each defended home court on Sunday with sterling defensive performances as two of the league's three best regular-season units. They put the two most recent WNBA champions into an early 0-1 deficit in the best-of-five series.

Despite failing to set the proper tone, they aren't flailing heading into Game 2s on Wednesday.

"We played like ass and only lost by 10," head coach Becky Hammon said following the No. 3 Las Vegas Aces' 71-60 loss to the Valkyries . "Dissect that however you want."

The Liberty could say the same, though first-year head coach Chris DeMarco rides a more insipid tact in press conferences. The No. 8-seeded Liberty dropped Game 1, 92-82, to No. 4 Atlanta on Sunday . After touching the ceiling of their long-awaited potential in the first-round sweep of No. 1 Minnesota, they dropped a few floors again in what's been a wild ride of a season.

The deficit felt larger amid a rocky third quarter of déjà vu mistakes that eventually ballooned into 16 points. The Liberty cut it to five three separate times in the final minutes, nearly cracking the younger, yet more composed Dream roster.

The Aces and Liberty have combined to win each of the past four championships. Las Vegas won three of them and is going for a second back-to-back run. They have the experience factor on their side. Yet each veteran roster committed the same macro problem: It didn't follow the game plan.

"All we talked about for the last 48 hours was rebounding and blocking them out, and we did not do it," Hammon said. "Period. I could end this whole thing right now, don't ask me about the game, it's rebounding. That was it. … But I'll take more questions."

The Valkyries doubled the Aces up on the boards, 52-25. They quadrupled their second-chance points (20-5). The four brought down by A'ja Wilson was one of her worst performances on the boards of the season. Valks center Kiah Stokes, her former teammate on two Aces title teams, held her to 2 of 10 from the floor as her primary defender, and only four baskets after the first quarter. Wilson's average field goal distance of 16.1 feet was the longest against any defender in the last five postseasons, per ESPN Insights .

Hammon described it as "one of our more atrocious games of the season," similar to her critical characterization of the first-round Game 2 loss to Indiana. They bounced back to win Game 3 at home to advance to the franchise's eighth consecutive semifinals.

New York's crew faced inquiries all week about live-ball turnovers and combating the steal-happy Dream's perimeter players. They faced each other twice two weeks ago in the final week of the regular season. They should have, and did, know the foe at hand.

"They have a lot of speed, and they're very good [at] — I don't want to call them gambles because they take the right risks when they do try to get steals," DeMarco said two hours before tipoff.

The Dream tied the WNBA postseason record for points off turnovers with 32 off 21. It provided one-third of their offense. Jordin Canada, namedropped by DeMarco as a defensive problem, had five steals.

And yet, the Liberty were still in it at the end enough that newly awarded Defensive Player of the Year Angel Reese wanted a timeout to settle her team and close out a win.

There aren't major changes for either of the losing teams to make to better match up. As Hammon has said in prior postseason runs, they can't adjust a game plan if they didn't actually follow it in the first place.

Game 2s are on Wednesday before each series shifts to the lower seeds. New York and Las Vegas will try to even the series before taking on home-court advantage. In last year's playoffs, the Mercury and Aces advanced to the WNBA Finals despite losing their semifinal openers.

Allisha Gray exited briefly in the first quarter with a left hand injury in front of her home bench. Dream head coach Karl Smesko had to call a timeout to have her seen on the bench before she left down the tunnel for the locker room. She returned, but reinjured it in the second quarter and immediately went down the tunnel. The team ruled her out for the remainder of the game.

Smesko said he did not have an update postgame.

"Obviously, she's been a huge reason we've been so successful this year, and it was tough to see her not out there," Smesko said. "But [I'm] really proud of how the team pulled together and how they played in the game."

Reese told reporters after the game that winning without Gray, their leading scorer at 19 points per game, "goes to show how talented our team is." DeWanna Bonner scored 23 on an efficient day in 30 minutes off the bench.

In Ballhalla, Jewell Loyd sustained a left leg injury early in the third quarter, the team said, and was ruled out. Hammon said she wasn't sure what happened. The veteran three-time champion missed two field goals in 16:34 as a starter in place of Stephanie Talbot, who did not play with a foot injury. In addition to going without NaLyssa Smith and Dana Evans, the Aces are playing with an ultra-short available rotation.

"You just gotta go with what's sitting on that bench," Hammon said. "Next woman up. Don't have a lot of time to sulk about it. Nobody feels bad for us."

articles.title: Ben Simmons' Kings Preseason Debut Timeline Revealed in NBA Rumors Ahead of Lakers, Warriors Games
articles.summary: Three-time All-Star Ben Simmons should suit up for the Sacramento Kings this week as they tip off the NBA preseason, according to Andscape's Marc J. Spears.
articles.body:
Three-time All-Star Ben Simmons should suit up for the Sacramento Kings this week as they tip off the NBA preseason, according to Andscape's Marc J. Spears .

Spears reported Simmons is likely to play Thursday against the Los Angeles Lakers or Saturday at the latest, when the Kings face off with the Golden State Warriors.

Simmons was out of the league for the 2025-26 season before signing a one-year deal with Sacramento. Prior to his hiatus, his value had hit a nadir.

Across 51 appearances with the Brooklyn Nets and Los Angeles Clippers, the veteran point guard averaged 5.0 points, 4.7 rebounds and 5.6 assists. During the Clippers' first-round playoff series with the Denver Nuggets, which stretched to seven games, he logged a total of 42 minutes.

Persistent back injuries derailed Simmons' career after he emerged as a two-way force for the Philadelphia 76ers. His lack of shooting range has always been a serious concern, but that didn't preclude him from earning All-NBA honors in 2019-20.

During the Kings' media day, the 30-year-old said it was "bulls--t" for people to assume he didn't have an earnest passion for basketball. He said his health was the biggest factor in him sitting out an entire season.

Sacramento should be an ideal place for Simmons to launch his comeback.

The Kings sit 29th in Bleacher Report's NBA power rankings after they finished 22-60 a year ago. They're unlikely to be a serious contender, which means Simmons should have plenty of playing time and the kind of role that allows him to show what he can do on the court.

With the preseason, he'll have the opportunity to shake off what will be a lot of rust.

articles.title: Darius Garland Hosts Call of Duty Competition for Clippers Teammates & Wants to Be Franchise Player
articles.summary: Darius Garland is ready to be the face of the Los Angeles Clippers as the franchise pivots away from the Kawhi Leonard era and faces life following the NBA's sanctions.
articles.body:
Darius Garland is ready to be the face of the Los Angeles Clippers as the franchise pivots away from the Kawhi Leonard era and faces life following the NBA's sanctions .

"I thought about it a little over the summertime," he told Marc J. Spears of Andscape. "It's definitely something I want. I've been through a lot in this career and I'm ready to take on the reins of that, especially in Year 8. I've actually found myself a little bit and I know where I want to get to. And that's a part of my plan, where I want to get better so I can get where I want to be. So, definitely, I'm ready for the opportunity."

That means taking on new leadership responsibilities. As Spears noted, Garland hosted a Call of Duty tournament for his teammates, went to a USC football game with teammate Kobe Sanders and a Los Angeles Rams game with rookie Keaton Wagler and spent much of the offseason working out and rehabbing at the team's practice facility.

"I'm definitely comfortable using my voice," Garland noted. "I just got to get used to using it all the time. I had a lot of good players that I had with me [in Cleveland] like [Donovan Mitchell]. But now I'm the head of the snake with the ball in my hands 99 percent of the time. So, I definitely got to dig down deep and actually get it out sometimes. That's the thing I'm working on right now."

articles.title: LeBron James' Helicopter Use With 76ers Part of Fanatics Contract, Details Surface in New NBA Rumors
articles.summary: LeBron James' endorsement deal with Fanatics includes on-demand helicopter service, according to Front Office Sports' Daniel Roberts and TMZ Sports.
articles.body:
LeBron James' endorsement deal with Fanatics includes on-demand helicopter service, according to Front Office Sports' Daniel Roberts and TMZ Sports .

Roberts noted that "a small handful of other athletes with big Fanatics deals get same access."

TMZ shared a photo of the Philadelphia 76ers star traveling in a Fanatics-branded chopper following the team's scrimmage on Saturday.

From the moment he signed with the Sixers, rumors surfaced that James intended to set up a home base in New York City and commute to Philadelphia on a helicopter. A one-way trip can be completed within an hour.

"The commute has invited outside curiosity but does not appear to faze anyone in the organization who are used to Sixers managing partner and primary owner Josh Harris coming and going the same way," ESPN's Dave McMenamin reported.

Of course, there's a difference between a member of ownership flying in from NYC and a player doing it.

The grind of the NBA schedule may require James to have some sort of living accommodations in the City of Brotherly Love. Staying in Philly makes more sense than going to New York when the Sixers have a home back-to-back.

The logistics of private air travel are much different and far more weather-dependent than commuting by car as well.

We've at least answered one question in terms of who's footing the bill for LeBron's expensive trips.

Michael Jordan made an eye-popping donation to his alma mater in honor of his mother, Deloris.

articles.title: Karl-Anthony Towns, Josh Hart Trades Teased by Shams in New Video amid Knicks Contract Rumors
articles.summary: The New York Knicks have maintained their desire to remain under the second tax apron, but it could cost them two of their best players.
articles.body:
The New York Knicks have maintained their desire to remain under the second tax apron, but it could cost them two of their best players.

During Monday's episode of NBA Today , ESPN's Shams Charania reported that Karl-Anthony Towns and Josh Hart could be trade candidates this season if they don't sign contract extensions soon.

"Josh Hart has already hinted that as this gets closer to February, which is around the trade deadline, the temperature could rise if Karl-Anthony Towns and Hart himself are not extended," Charania said. "So far, these sides are not close."

Towns is eligible for a four-year deal worth over $276 million, while Hart is eligible for a four-year, $131.2 million deal. While both players were instrumental in leading the Knicks to their first NBA championship since 1973, team owner James Dolan has been adamant that he will not go into the second spending apron.

Towns reiterated on Monday that he and the Knicks are not close on an extension despite his willingness to take a team-friendly deal.

"Simply put – I want to do something to keep the team together and can work with the Knicks and also values me. And none of those things are close to happening," Towns told reporters .

When asked if he thought winning a championship would facilitate negotiations for a new deal, Towns said , "No s--t, Sherlock. I just won a championship. You'd think it was pretty easy. Unless you guys [reporters] think I have something else to prove."

It sounds like the Knicks are running the risk of making some of their top stars unhappy. While it's important to maintain good salary cap health, the team's chemistry was unmatched last season.

With the start of the 2026-27 season approaching on Oct. 20, the Knicks are running out of time to eliminate the distractions and resolve their contract situations with Towns and Hart.

articles.title: Joel Embiid's Updated Weight Revealed in New NBA Rumors Since LeBron James' Arrival to 76ers
articles.summary: It hasn't been much of a secret that Joel Embiid showed up to the Philadelphia 76ers' training camp looking far slimmer than in years past after finally being healthy enough in the offseason to focus on training and conditioning rather than injury rehab.
articles.body:
It hasn't been much of a secret that Joel Embiid showed up to the Philadelphia 76ers' training camp looking far slimmer than in years past after finally being healthy enough in the offseason to focus on training and conditioning rather than injury rehab.

On Monday, ESPN's Ramona Shelburne offered more details on the superstar center's physical transformation.

"I've been hearing Embiid's getting to the gym early, he's down to his rookie weight, this is a new Joel," she said on NBA Today . "Everybody's trying to kind of earn LeBron James' approval and respect. I think there's an interesting quality to this now in Philly. I saw this here in Los Angeles in 2020, when Anthony Davis and James first got together for that full season, they won a championship. Davis was like trying to impress LeBron. Like, he played every game, There was a tide lift amongst the stars too with the James' effect. That's what I've been hearing out of Philly so far is this sort of, LeBron is one of the greatest of all time, if not the greatest, and everybody kind of wants his approval."

James brings an unmatched pedigree to Philadelphia, no doubt, although the desire to win a championship is strong for Embiid regardless of the King's presence.

LeBron has said he's hoping to be the " final little piece " that helps Embiid get a championship, comments that Embiid appreciated.

"You're talking about one of the greatest players to ever play, if not the greatest. To have him say that, in kinda validates—not so much what I've accomplished, but the way my peers think about me," he told ESPN's Malika Andrews (3:30 mark). "I'm at the point in my career where I just want, I need to win. Between everything that's happened, that would be a good ending for the city of Philadelphia and they deserve it."

But with a healthy offseason, the 32-year-old Embiid has also helped his own cause, and folks in Philadelphia have taken notice.

"We got a plan together, and he's been in every single drill, every single practice," president of basketball operations Mike Gansey told reporters while discussing the team's plans for keeping Embiid healthy this season. "So there's been no restrictions. Obviously, worked super hard this summer. He told me he was motivated. He wanted to have a great year, and he's showing it out there. Looks a little bit lighter, obviously, but the skill level is still there. I mean, some of the stuff he does now seeing it in person, like it's incredible to watch some of the stuff he does on the floor. So we're excited about him, and he's been good this first week."

A healthy Embiid, plus the additions of James and Jaylen Brown and the return of Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe has the potential to be special. There is plenty to figure out from a chemistry and roles perspective, but the talent on hand is absurd.

articles.title: Jason Kidd Eyed by ESPN for TV Role After Mavs Exit, New NBA Rumors Reveal Details
articles.summary: Jason Kidd's next job in the basketball world reportedly could be on television.
articles.body:
Jason Kidd's next job in the basketball world reportedly could be on television.

NBA insider Marc Stein reported Monday that ESPN has reached "advanced talks" with the former coach and the Dallas Mavericks mutually parting ways in May. According to Stein, Kidd's role would be with the network's studio coverage.

It is a new era in Dallas, as it hired Masai Ujiri as team president this offseason.

The Mavericks announced their mutual parting of ways with Kidd fewer than three weeks after hiring Ujiri. Stein reported at the time the team wanted a "clean slate" in a new era.

ESPN's Tim MacMahon reported on the situation as well, noting Kidd expressed interest in becoming the team's president of basketball operations following the firing of general manager Nico Harrison.

However, Mavericks governor Patrick Dumont told the coach he wouldn't be considered for that role. What's more, MacMahon reported Kidd—who had four years and more than $40 million left on his deal when he parted ways with the team—was not part of the process that resulted in Ujiri's hiring.

Both Kidd and the Mavericks are heading in different directions with the Western Conference team hiring Dusty May as their new head coach.

And Kidd figures to bring an experienced perspective to ESPN's coverage. After all, he was a Hall of Fame player before he was a coach and amassed a resume that included a championship, a Rookie of the Year, five assist titles, six All-NBA selections and 10 All-Star nods.

He was also included on the NBA's 75th Anniversary Team.

In addition to his five seasons as the head coach of the Mavericks, Kidd coached the Brooklyn Nets, Milwaukee Bucks and Los Angeles Lakers.

articles.title: Karl-Anthony Towns' Top Trade Landing Spots After Knicks Star's Contract Remarks Amid NBA Rumors
articles.summary: The New York Knicks spent much of their offseason celebrating their first title in 53 years, but they now have to deal with the less desirable parts of having a championship-contending roster.
articles.body:
The New York Knicks spent much of their offseason celebrating their first title in 53 years, but they now have to deal with the less desirable parts of having a championship-contending roster.

The Knicks and star center Karl-Anthony Towns have been back and forth on a new contract over the last few months, with the team reportedly offering him a $200 million deal, which is $77 million less than his max.

Towns recently outlined what he's looking for in a new deal and said , "None of those things are close to happening." When asked whether he thought it'd be easy to get a deal done after helping lead the Knicks to a title, Towns said, "No s--t, Sherlock. I just won a championship. You'd think it was pretty easy. Unless you guys think I have something else to prove."

The idea of Towns leaving the Knicks in June would have been unfathomable, but it appears to be at least an option at this point if negotiations don't improve, as ESPN's Shams Charania teased the possibility on Monday. If New York decides to trade its star big man, here are some potential landing spots.

The Washington Wizards appear to be a team on the rise in the East, but it's no secret that Anthony Davis might not be a long-term option in the frontcourt.

Davis told reporters last week that he'll decide on his player option after the 2026-27 campaign, so the Wizards could be in a tricky situation if he decides to enter free agency and leave Washington next summer.

With Davis not being fully committed to the future, the Wizards could consider trading him to New York in return for Towns, who might be on board with signing a long-term deal in Washington for the right price.

It would be a win-win for both teams, as the Knicks would get a center that could help them stay relevant, while the Wizards would get a player with championship experience to replace Davis.

Towns would also fit in well alongside Trae Young and top draft pick AJ Dybantsa.

Stephen Curry inked an extension with the Warriors that is $20 million less than what he was eligible for, and the front office now has the chance to reward him by building a championship-contending roster around him.

After missing out on Giannis Antetokounmpo and Jaylen Brown this summer, Golden State could make a splash elsewhere by trading for Towns.

The biggest question mark in this scenario is whether the Warriors have the draft capital to land an All-Star big man like Towns. It's unclear if Jimmy Butler and/or Draymond Green would be involved, but Golden State's best package would likely include Kristaps Porziņģis and a handful of draft picks.

The Warriors might have to sacrifice their future a bit by trading picks, but it could be a worthwhile investment if it means getting one last title before the end of Curry's career.

As it stands now, the Cleveland Cavaliers are set to enter the 2026-27 campaign with the same core they had last year.

With a star center potentially on the trade block, the Cavs' front office should reconsider whether that's the right plan of attack.

Cleveland has been on the brink of competing for a title over the last few years, but continues to fall short. The addition of James Harden last year helped the Cavs reach the conference finals, but they ultimately didn't have enough to get over the hump.

The team is built around Donovan Mitchell, and that isn't going to change, but the Cavs could look into trading Evan Mobley for Towns or package Jarrett Allen with a handful of role players or picks.

The latter would probably be the more favorable option since Mobley is just 25 years old and is entering his prime.

articles.body:
The Golden State Valkyries are turning San Francisco's Chase Center into a celebrity hotspot as they continue to dominate their first postseason run.

"Star Wars" creator George Lucas, comedian Ali Wong, rapper E-40 and Grammy Award-winning singer Kehlani were among the local stars at Ballhalla to cheer on the team over the weekend.

"Actually, it's my first time and that's not my fault, I'm a busy girl," Kehlani said in a video posted to Chase Center's Instagram account on Sunday, Oct. 4. "But I would love to come all the time and I'm so thoroughly impressed and so proud that we have a team."

The "Folded" singer was back in the Bay Area to close her self-titled tour with two shows at Mountain View's Shoreline Amphitheatre on Saturday and Sunday, Oct. 3-4. The Oakland native brought out Fresno singer Ezra, San Francisco rapper Karri, Vallejo rap collective SOBxRBE and her 7-year-old daughter Adeya as surprise guests during her live performances.

While watching the Valkyries take on the Las Vegas Aces before her Sunday concert, Kehlani took selfies with the team's mascot, Violet, and several players. She also posed for a photo on the court with San Francisco DJ Noodles, a frequent tour collaborator.

For Wong's part, the San Francisco native took a break from her ongoing comedy tour to sound the ceremonial drum before Sunday's game. Unlike Kehlani, Wong has been spotted at several Valkyries games since the WNBA team launched last year.

The Valkyries won 71-60 over the Aces. The two teams face off again for Game 2 of the semifinals on Wednesday, Oct. 6, at Chase Center.

Other stars in attendance at Sunday's game included Olympic swimmer Natalia Coughlin; Meena Harris, niece of former Vice President Kamala Harris; and content creator Brittany Hampton.

Before Sunday's celebrity-filled game, Friday, Oct. 2, drew its own notable crowd. Lucas made a rare public appearance at Game 3 of the Valkyries' first-round WNBA playoff series against the Dallas Wings with his wife, Mellody Hobson. The Valkyries won 77-73 to make the semifinals.

The couple recently opened the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art in Los Angeles, which showcases an array of paintings, photography, sculptures, comic art and more.

Vallejo rapper E-40, a regular at Golden State Warriors games, was also spotted Friday.

Prior to that, fellow Bay Area rapper Too Short attended the franchise's first-ever home playoff game, Game 1 of the first round against the Wings on Sept. 27, and performed live during halftime.

Fans can likely expect more celebrity appearances at Ballhalla as the Valkyries continue to vie for this year's championship trophy. The WNBA Finals are scheduled to begin on Oct. 17.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark faces scrutiny over alleged response to Sydney Colson incident
articles.summary: ifeelstock/Depositphotos What really happened between Clark and Colson Caitlin Clark and former Indiana Fever teammate Sydney Colson are at the center of a n...
articles.body:
What really happened between Clark and Colson

Caitlin Clark and former Indiana Fever teammate Sydney Colson are at the center of a new social-media controversy after an alleged Instagram unfollow drew attention following Indiana's playoff game against Las Vegas. The speculation grew after Colson became involved in a tense courtside exchange during the September 29 matchup.

The situation has since fueled theories of a possible rift between the former teammates, with fans also citing Colson's earlier comments about a controversial foul involving Clark. But did the two incidents actually have anything to do with each other?

Indiana defeated Las Vegas 99-89 in Game 2 of the WNBA first-round series on September 29. Caitlin Clark recorded 27 points, 15 assists and 7 rebounds as Indiana tied the best-of-three series.

During the fourth quarter, A'ja Wilson confronted a Fever fan after a play involving Sophie Cunningham. Wilson received a technical foul, while teammates, officials and security personnel separated those involved.

Sydney Colson was shown approaching the area where Wilson and a fan were involved in the confrontation. Video showed Colson speaking toward a spectator, although the full context of the exchange was not established in available reports.

Colson was at the game as a broadcaster after spending the 2025 season with Indiana. She and Wilson previously played together for Las Vegas and won WNBA championships with the Aces in 2022 and 2023.

Early reports suggested the fan involved in the confrontation had been ejected from Gainbridge Fieldhouse. The Indiana Fever later said security spoke with the fan and witnesses and found no Fan Code of Conduct violation.

The team said the fan was not removed from the arena and that it considered the matter closed. The clarification differed from reports that circulated immediately after the incident.

Colson did not play for Indiana during the 2026 season and entered free agency after her one-year Fever contract ended. USA Today reported in August that she was recovering from the ACL injury that ended her 2025 season.

Her 2026 work included broadcasting and analysis related to women's basketball. She was at the playoff game as part of Amazon's WNBA coverage rather than appearing as an active Fever player.

Colson joined the Fever in 2025 as a veteran guard who could back up Clark and provide experience. She appeared in 30 games and started six before suffering a left knee ACL tear on August 7, 2025.

Clark and Colson shared a professional relationship during Indiana's 2025 season. No verified report establishes a personal dispute connected to the September 29 courtside incident.

The earlier Thomas controversy resurfaced

Colson drew attention in June after discussing Alyssa Thomas' contact with Clark during an ESPN segment. She said she did not believe the play should have been a Flagrant 2 and described the WNBA as physical.

The WNBA later assessed Thomas a Flagrant Foul 2 and suspended her for 1 game. The league said Thomas had recklessly made contact with Clark's throat area with her fist during the June 24 game.

Interesting fact : Caitlin Clark was the No. 1 overall pick in the 2024 WNBA Draft. The Indiana Fever selected her first overall after her record-setting college career at Iowa.

Clark later said she believed the Thomas play was a flagrant foul and that the league needed to do better protecting players. Her comments came after the WNBA reviewed the incident and announced Thomas' suspension.

That position differed from Colson's televised assessment. No verified public statement from Clark says Colson's June comments caused the alleged social-media change reported after the September game.

Interesting fact : Sydney Colson is a two-time WNBA champion.

A September 30 report said Clark's Instagram account did not follow Colson and that Colson continued following Clark. The report attributed the unfollow claim to an X user, but a visible Instagram follow list cannot establish when or why a change occurred.

No direct statement from Clark confirms that she unfollowed Colson because of the September 29 confrontation. The available reporting therefore does not establish a connection between the alleged Instagram change and the courtside incident.

Social-media users connected the alleged unfollow to the September confrontation and Colson's earlier comments about the Thomas incident. Those reactions are documented online, but they represent individual users rather than verified statements from Clark or the Fever.

Some posts described the alleged unfollow as evidence of a personal disagreement. No reliable public evidence establishes that interpretation, so it should not be presented as confirmed.

Clark's playoff performance remained central

Amid the discussion, Clark produced a major performance in Game 2 against Las Vegas. She finished with 27 points, 15 assists and 7 rebounds as Indiana won 99-89 and tied the series.

The WNBA's official box score confirms Clark played 33 minutes and made 9 of 18 field-goal attempts. She also made 5 three-pointers and committed 5 turnovers.

Indiana's victory forced Game 3 in Las Vegas after the teams split the opening two games. Game 3 was played October 1 at Michelob ULTRA Arena in the best-of-three first round.

Las Vegas defeated Indiana 94-83 in Game 3 to win the series 2-1 and advance to the WNBA semifinals. The September 29 confrontation was documented through video and game reporting, while the alleged Instagram unfollow remained unconfirmed by Clark.

Clark's latest game came at a crucial point in the Fever's season, with their playoff hopes hanging in the balance. Check out how she responded in Caitlin Clark reacts to early third-quarter exit as Fever near elimination .

Reporting confirms Colson became involved in the courtside exchange during Indiana's September 29 playoff game. A September 30 report said Clark did not follow Colson on Instagram and that an X user had claimed Clark unfollowed her.

No direct statement from Clark confirms that she intentionally unfollowed Colson because of the incident. The record establishes Indiana's Game 2 win, the courtside confrontation and the online claim, but not a connection between the alleged Instagram change and the confrontation.

articles.title: Max Strus will miss start of season for Clippers due to latest foot injury
articles.summary: Max Strus suffered a partial tear of the plantar fascia in his right foot, and will be evaluated again in four weeks.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Clippers guard Max Strus will be out for at least a month with a foot injury.

Strus left Sunday's preseason win over the Golden State Warriors in Hawaii early after about five minutes after he pulled up with a non-contact injury. He limped off to the locker room and didn't return.

The team announced on Monday that Strus suffered a partial tear of the plantar fascia in his right foot. He'll be reevaluated again in four weeks, meaning he will miss at least the start of the regular season.

Strus averaged 11.2 points and 5.4 rebounds last season with the Cleveland Cavaliers, though he played in only 12 games while dealing with a broken left foot . He was traded to the Clippers in August in a three-team deal that sent Peyton Watson to the Cavaliers.

Strus is in the final year of a four-year, $62 million deal he first signed with the Cavaliers before the 2023-24 campaign. He appeared in only 50 games during the 2024-25 season, and has played in more than 70 games a year only twice in his seven-year career in the league.

The injury is just the latest significant one for the Clippers this offseason. Forward Brandon Ingram has a partially torn Achilles tendon , and will also miss the start of the season. It's not clear how long Ingram will be sidelined, but the team expects he could need about six fewer months of rehab than he would if it were a full Achilles tear.

Ingram was acquired in the trade that sent Kawhi Leonard to the Toronto Raptors, which was finally completed last month after the conclusion of the NBA's investigation into the Clippers over salary-cap circumvention regarding Leonard . The Clippers also got Gradey Dick and unprotected first-round picks in 2031 and 2033 in the deal.

The Clippers will open the regular season at home against the Sacramento Kings on Oct. 21. While Strus' injury doesn't sound anywhere near as significant as Ingram's, he will now not be able to make his debut with the franchise until early November, at best.
